gita-4-17.meaning: There is right action, wrong action and non-action. Telling them apart takes real understanding.
gita-4-17.explanation: Krishna names three things to understand: proper action, wrong or forbidden action, and inaction. The ways of karma are subtle, so careful thought is needed.

gita-4-18.translation: One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is wise among people. Such a person is steady in yoga, even while doing every kind of work.
gita-4-18.meaning: A wise person can be busy outwardly yet still within, and sees that doing nothing can also be a choice.
gita-4-18.explanation: This paradox is at the heart of the chapter. Acting without attachment is really a kind of stillness, while avoiding duty out of fear is still a kind of action. Seeing this clearly is true wisdom.

gita-4-19.translation: One whose every undertaking is free from desire and self-centred motive, whose actions are burned up in the fire of knowledge, is called wise by the wise.
gita-4-19.meaning: A true sage acts without selfish wants. Knowledge burns away the hold actions would otherwise have.
gita-4-19.explanation: Krishna describes the sage: their projects are free of craving and selfish plans, and knowledge has burned away the binding power of their deeds. The wise call such a person truly learned.

gita-4-20.translation: Giving up attachment to the results of action, always content and depending on nothing, such a person does nothing at all, even while fully engaged in action.
gita-4-20.meaning: When you are content and not clinging to results, your work no longer binds you.
gita-4-20.explanation: Krishna continues the portrait. Someone who has dropped clinging to outcomes, who is content and leans on nothing outside, is in a deep sense not acting, even while very active.

keywords.meaning: attachment to the fruit of action

gita-4-21.translation: Expecting nothing, with mind and self under control, having given up all possessiveness, doing only bodily work, such a person incurs no fault.
gita-4-21.meaning: Someone who wants nothing and holds onto nothing can work and stay free of wrongdoing.
gita-4-21.explanation: A person without cravings, self-controlled and free of possessiveness, does only what the body needs to do. Such action brings no sin, because it is not driven by greed.

gita-4-22.translation: Content with whatever comes by itself, beyond the pairs of opposites, free of envy, the same in success and failure, such a person is not bound even while acting.
gita-4-22.meaning: Be happy with what comes, rise above likes and dislikes, and stay calm whether you win or lose.
gita-4-22.explanation: Krishna lists more marks of one who is free: content with what comes unsought, beyond pairs like heat and cold or praise and blame, without jealousy, steady in success and failure. Such a person acts but is not bound.

gita-4-23.translation: For one who is free of attachment, liberated, whose mind is set in knowledge, and who acts as an offering, all action dissolves completely.
gita-4-23.meaning: When work is done as an offering, without clinging, it leaves no trace that binds.
gita-4-23.explanation: When action is done for the sake of sacrifice by one who is free and grounded in knowledge, it melts away and leaves no bondage. This leads into the verses on sacrifice that follow.

gita-4-24.translation: The offering is Brahman, the ghee is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire that is Brahman. One who sees Brahman in every action reaches Brahman.
gita-4-24.meaning: See God in everything: the giver, the gift, the act of giving and the goal. Then all of life becomes holy.
gita-4-24.explanation: This verse is often chanted before meals. Every part of the ritual, the offering, the butter, the fire and the one offering, is seen as the one reality, Brahman. One who sees this in all action goes to Brahman.

gita-4-25.translation: Some yogis offer sacrifice to the gods. Others offer the sacrifice itself into the fire of Brahman.
gita-4-25.meaning: People worship in different ways. Some pray to the gods, others offer themselves to the Supreme.
gita-4-25.explanation: Krishna begins listing many kinds of sacrifice. Some yogis perform worship directed to the gods. Others make a deeper offering, giving up the self into the fire of the Absolute.

gita-4-26.translation: Some offer hearing and the other senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sound and the other sense objects into the fires of the senses.
gita-4-26.meaning: Some people grow by holding the senses back. Others by using the senses in a pure way.
gita-4-26.explanation: Krishna describes two kinds of inner sacrifice. Some restrain the senses, offering them into the fire of self-control. Others let the senses meet their objects, but offer that experience as a sacrifice.

gita-4-27.translation: Others offer all the actions of the senses and of the life-breath into the fire of self-control, lit by knowledge.
gita-4-27.meaning: Some people give all their senses and energies into the fire of self-mastery.
gita-4-27.explanation: Another kind of sacrifice is complete inner discipline. All sense activity and all movements of the life force are offered into the yoga of self-control, a fire kindled by knowledge.

gita-4-28.translation: Others offer wealth, austerity or yoga as sacrifice; and some, self-controlled and firm in their vows, offer study of scripture and knowledge.
gita-4-28.meaning: Giving money, living simply, practising yoga and studying wisdom can all be forms of sacrifice.
gita-4-28.explanation: Krishna continues the list. Giving wealth, practising austerity, practising yoga, and quiet study leading to knowledge are all sacrifices. Those who do them are disciplined and keep strict vows.

gita-4-29.translation: Others offer the out-breath into the in-breath and the in-breath into the out-breath, controlling both, devoted to the regulation of breath.
gita-4-29.meaning: Some people use the breath itself as their practice, calming and guiding each breath.
gita-4-29.explanation: This describes pranayama, breath control. Practitioners offer one breath into the other and hold the flow of both. Mastering the breath is presented as a form of sacrifice.

gita-4-30.translation: Others, eating with restraint, offer their life-breaths into life-breaths. All of these know sacrifice, and through sacrifice their faults are destroyed.
gita-4-30.meaning: Even eating mindfully can be a sacrifice. Every sincere practice cleanses the person who does it.
gita-4-30.explanation: Some practise moderation in food as their offering. Krishna sums up: all these people truly understand sacrifice, and through it their faults are washed away.

gita-4-31.translation: Those who eat what remains of sacrifice, the nectar, reach eternal Brahman. This world is not for one who makes no sacrifice, let alone the next, O best of the Kurus.
gita-4-31.meaning: Those who live by giving reach God. Someone who never gives finds no happiness here or beyond.
gita-4-31.explanation: Taking only what is left after offering is called eating nectar, and it leads to Brahman. A life without any sacrifice brings no good even in this world, much less in the next.

keywords.meaning: of one who does not sacrifice

gita-4-32.translation: Many kinds of sacrifice are set out in this way in the Vedas. Know that all of them are born of action. Knowing this, you will be free.
gita-4-32.meaning: All these sacrifices involve action. Understanding this sets you free.
gita-4-32.explanation: Krishna concludes the list: the Vedas describe many forms of sacrifice. All of them come from action. Knowing that action itself can be an offering is what liberates.

keywords.meaning: in the mouth of the Veda

gita-4-33.translation: The sacrifice of knowledge is better than any sacrifice of material things, O scorcher of foes. All action, without exception, finds its completion in knowledge, Arjuna.
gita-4-33.meaning: Gaining true wisdom is the greatest offering. Every action finally leads to knowledge.
gita-4-33.explanation: Among all sacrifices, the offering of knowledge is the highest. Material offerings are good, but every action finds its fulfilment in wisdom.

gita-4-34.translation: Learn this by bowing down, by asking questions and by serving. The wise who have seen the truth will teach you knowledge.
gita-4-34.meaning: To learn deep truth, find a wise teacher. Approach with humility, sincere questions and service.
gita-4-34.explanation: Krishna describes how to gain knowledge: humble respect, honest inquiry and service to a teacher. Those who have seen the truth will then share it. Humility and curiosity go together.

gita-4-35.translation: Knowing this, you will never fall into such confusion again, Pandava. By it you will see all beings in yourself, and then in me.
gita-4-35.meaning: With true knowledge, confusion ends. You will see everyone as part of yourself and of God.
gita-4-35.explanation: Krishna promises that with this knowledge Arjuna's present confusion will not return. He will see all beings in his own Self and that Self in Krishna. The whole of life becomes one.

gita-4-36.translation: Even if you were the worst of all sinners, you would cross over all wrongdoing by the boat of knowledge alone.
gita-4-36.meaning: No matter what you have done, wisdom can carry you past it like a boat over a river.
gita-4-36.explanation: This is a verse of great hope. Even the worst wrongdoer can cross the ocean of sin using the raft of knowledge. No one is beyond redemption.

gita-4-37.translation: Just as a blazing fire turns firewood to ashes, Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge turns all actions to ashes.
gita-4-37.meaning: Wisdom burns away the hold of past actions, like fire burns wood.
gita-4-37.explanation: Krishna gives a vivid image. As fire reduces fuel to ash, the fire of knowledge burns up the binding effects of all action. Past karma loses its grip.

gita-4-38.translation: Truly there is nothing in this world as purifying as knowledge. One who is perfected in yoga finds it within himself in time.
gita-4-38.meaning: Nothing cleans the heart like true wisdom. With steady practice, you discover it within.
gita-4-38.explanation: Knowledge is the greatest purifier. It is not just learned from outside: one who matures in yoga discovers it in the Self, in due course.

gita-4-39.translation: One who has faith, who is devoted to it and who controls the senses gains knowledge. Having gained it, that person soon reaches supreme peace.
gita-4-39.meaning: Faith, dedication and self-control lead to wisdom, and wisdom quickly brings deep peace.
gita-4-39.explanation: Krishna names three conditions for knowledge: faith, wholehearted dedication, and mastery of the senses. Once knowledge comes, the highest peace follows quickly.

gita-4-40.translation: But the ignorant one, without faith and full of doubt, is lost. For the doubting soul there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
gita-4-40.meaning: Constant doubt, without faith, leaves a person with no peace anywhere.
gita-4-40.explanation: Krishna warns about the opposite. A person who lacks knowledge and faith and is eaten by doubt is ruined. Endless doubt brings no happiness here or hereafter.

gita-4-41.translation: Actions do not bind one who has given up action through yoga, who has cut through doubt with knowledge, and who is centred in the Self, Dhananjaya.
gita-4-41.meaning: When you work selflessly, clear your doubts with wisdom and stay grounded within, your actions no longer bind you.
gita-4-41.explanation: Krishna brings together yoga and knowledge. Offering action through yoga, cutting doubt with knowledge, and being established in the Self: such a person is not bound by karma.

keywords.meaning: one who has given up action through yoga

gita-4-42.translation: So cut away this doubt in your heart, born of ignorance, with the sword of knowledge. Take refuge in yoga. Stand up, Arjuna!
gita-4-42.meaning: Use wisdom like a sword to cut through doubt, then rise and do what you must.
gita-4-42.explanation: The chapter ends with a call to action. Arjuna's doubt comes from ignorance and lives in his heart. He should cut it away with the sword of knowledge, stand firm in yoga, and rise to his duty.

gita-5-1.translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, you praise giving up action, and then you praise yoga through action. Tell me clearly which of the two is better.
gita-5-1.meaning: Arjuna is confused: should he give up action or act selflessly? He asks for one clear answer.
gita-5-1.explanation: Krishna has praised both renouncing action and acting in yoga. Arjuna wants a single, definite answer about which path is better for him. The fifth chapter is Krishna's reply.

gita-5-2.translation: Krishna said: Renouncing action and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good. But of the two, the yoga of action is better than renouncing action.
gita-5-2.meaning: Both paths lead to freedom, but working selflessly is better than quitting work.
gita-5-2.explanation: Krishna answers directly. Both paths lead to liberation, but acting without attachment is better than simply giving up action. It is more practical and keeps the person engaged with the world.

gita-5-3.translation: Know that person as a true renunciate who neither hates nor desires. Free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, such a person is easily freed from bondage.
gita-5-3.meaning: A true renunciate is not someone who leaves home, but someone free of hatred and craving.
gita-5-3.explanation: Krishna redefines renunciation. It is an inner state: having no hatred and no craving, beyond opposites like pleasure and pain. Such a person is a renunciate even while working, and is easily freed.

gita-5-4.translation: The childish, not the wise, say that knowledge and the yoga of action are different. One who is truly established in either gains the fruit of both.
gita-5-4.meaning: The path of knowledge and the path of action are not rivals. Following one sincerely brings the result of both.
gita-5-4.explanation: Krishna says only the immature see Sankhya, the path of knowledge, and Yoga, the path of action, as separate. Anyone fully established in one receives the fruit of both.

gita-5-5.translation: The state reached by the followers of knowledge is reached by the followers of action too. One who sees that knowledge and action are one truly sees.
gita-5-5.meaning: Both paths reach the same goal. Seeing this is real understanding.
gita-5-5.explanation: Krishna repeats the point with emphasis: the destination is the same for those who follow knowledge and those who follow selfless action. True sight is seeing these as one.

gita-5-6.translation: But renunciation is hard to attain without yoga, O mighty-armed. The sage who is steady in yoga quickly reaches Brahman.
gita-5-6.meaning: Trying to renounce without first acting selflessly is very hard. Selfless action quickly leads to God.
gita-5-6.explanation: Krishna explains why action comes first. Giving up action is difficult without the training of selfless work. A sage who practises yoga reaches Brahman without delay.

gita-5-7.translation: One who is steady in yoga, pure in heart, master of mind and senses, whose self has become the self of all beings, is not stained even while acting.
gita-5-7.meaning: When you see yourself in everyone and control your mind, your actions do not bind you.
gita-5-7.explanation: Krishna describes the yogi who is pure, self-controlled and sees his own Self in all beings. Such a person acts but remains untouched by the effects of action.

keywords.meaning: whose self is the self of all beings

gita-5-8.translation: The one steady in yoga, who knows the truth, thinks, 'I do nothing at all,' even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping and breathing.
gita-5-8.meaning: A wise person knows the real Self does not do the everyday actions of the body.
gita-5-8.explanation: Krishna describes the inner attitude of the knower. While the body sees, hears, eats, walks, sleeps and breathes, the knower remembers the Self is not the doer.

gita-5-9.translation: While speaking, letting go, grasping, opening and closing the eyes, such a person holds that only the senses are moving among their objects.
gita-5-9.meaning: The senses do their work, but the true Self stays a calm witness.
gita-5-9.explanation: Continuing the thought, Krishna says that during all bodily activities the wise one sees them as the senses engaging their objects, not as the Self acting.

gita-5-10.translation: One who acts, offering all actions to Brahman and giving up attachment, is not touched by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not wet by water.
gita-5-10.meaning: Offer your work to God and let go of clinging. Then wrongdoing will not stick to you, like water on a lotus leaf.
gita-5-10.explanation: This is one of the Gita's best-known images. The lotus grows in water but its leaf stays dry. In the same way, someone who offers every action to the divine lives in the world without being stained by it.

gita-5-11.translation: Yogis act with body, mind, intellect and even the senses alone, giving up attachment, for the purification of the self.
gita-5-11.meaning: Selfless people work with body and mind only to purify themselves, not for personal gain.
gita-5-11.explanation: Yogis keep acting, using body, mind, intellect and senses, but without attachment. The purpose of their work is inner cleansing, not personal reward.

gita-5-12.translation: The one steady in yoga, giving up the fruit of action, reaches lasting peace. The unsteady, driven by desire and attached to the fruit, are bound.
gita-5-12.meaning: Letting go of results brings peace. Working only for results keeps you tied up.
gita-5-12.explanation: Krishna contrasts two people. One gives up attachment to results and finds lasting peace. The other, pushed by desire and clinging to outcomes, remains bound.

keywords.meaning: giving up the fruit of action

gita-5-13.translation: Having renounced all actions with the mind, the embodied self rests happily in the city of nine gates, neither acting nor causing others to act.
gita-5-13.meaning: The true Self lives in the body like a calm master in a city, untouched by its busy activity.
gita-5-13.explanation: The body is pictured as a city with nine gates: two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, the mouth and the two lower openings. The Self, having let go inwardly, lives there in peace, neither acting nor making others act.

keywords.meaning: in the city of nine gates

gita-5-14.translation: The Lord does not create the sense of being the doer, nor actions, nor the link between action and its fruit. It is nature that does all this.
gita-5-14.meaning: God does not make us act or make us feel we are the doers. That comes from our own nature.
gita-5-14.explanation: Krishna explains that the sense of agency, actions themselves and their results are not created by the Lord. They arise from nature, the field of matter and its qualities, working by its own laws.

gita-5-15.translation: The all-pervading Lord does not take on anyone's sin or good deeds. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and so beings are deluded.
gita-5-15.meaning: God does not take credit or blame for our actions. We become confused when ignorance hides the truth.
gita-5-15.explanation: The Lord is not responsible for anyone's good or bad actions. People are confused because their true knowledge is covered by ignorance, like the sun behind clouds.

gita-5-16.translation: But for those whose ignorance has been destroyed by knowledge of the Self, that knowledge shines like the sun and reveals the Supreme.
gita-5-16.meaning: When wisdom removes ignorance, the truth shines clearly, like the sun.
gita-5-16.explanation: When ignorance is removed by self-knowledge, knowledge lights everything up like the sun. It reveals the highest reality.

gita-5-17.translation: Those whose minds are on That, whose self is in That, who are rooted in That and hold That as their goal, go to the state of no return, their faults washed away by knowledge.
gita-5-17.meaning: Fill your mind and heart with God. Then you reach the state from which there is no falling back.
gita-5-17.explanation: Krishna describes total absorption in the Supreme: thinking of it, identifying with it, resting in it, devoted to it. Such people, cleansed by knowledge, attain freedom from rebirth.

gita-5-19.translation: Even here, the world of birth is conquered by those whose minds rest in sameness. Brahman is flawless and the same in all, so they are established in Brahman.
gita-5-19.meaning: Seeing everyone as equal is a kind of victory over the world, here and now.
gita-5-19.explanation: Following the verse on seeing the same Self in a scholar, a cow, an elephant and a dog, Krishna says those whose minds are established in equality have conquered rebirth even in this life. Brahman is pure and the same everywhere, so they rest in Brahman.

gita-5-20.translation: One who knows Brahman and rests in Brahman, with steady understanding and free from delusion, does not rejoice at getting what is pleasant nor grieve at getting what is unpleasant.
gita-5-20.meaning: A wise person stays calm, not overjoyed by good news nor crushed by bad news.
gita-5-20.explanation: The knower of Brahman has a steady mind and is free from delusion. Pleasant and unpleasant events come, but they do not throw them into elation or despair.

gita-5-21.translation: One not attached to outer contacts finds joy within. Joined to Brahman through yoga, that person enjoys happiness that never ends.
gita-5-21.meaning: Real happiness comes from within, not from outside things, and it lasts forever.
gita-5-21.explanation: When a person stops depending on sense contacts for happiness, they find joy inside. United with Brahman by yoga, they taste happiness that does not fade.

gita-5-22.translation: Pleasures born of contact with sense objects are sources of pain. They have a beginning and an end, Arjuna. The wise do not delight in them.
gita-5-22.meaning: Pleasures from the senses come and go, and they often lead to pain. The wise do not chase them.
gita-5-22.explanation: Sense pleasures start and stop. Because they end, and because we crave them, they become sources of sorrow. The wise do not build their happiness on them.

gita-5-23.translation: One who can withstand the force of desire and anger here, before leaving the body, is a yogi and a happy person.
gita-5-23.meaning: If you can master desire and anger while you live, you are truly happy.
gita-5-23.explanation: Krishna sets a practical test. Whoever can bear the surge of desire and anger in this life, before death, is a real yogi and truly happy.

gita-5-24.translation: One whose happiness is within, whose joy is within, whose light is within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman.
gita-5-24.meaning: Find your happiness, joy and light inside. That leads to the peace of God.
gita-5-24.explanation: Here Krishna describes the inward-turned yogi: their happiness, delight and illumination are all inside. Such a person becomes Brahman and attains the peace of Brahman, often called nirvana.

gita-5-25.translation: Sages whose sins are destroyed, whose doubts are cut away, who are self-controlled and who delight in the good of all beings, attain the peace of Brahman.
gita-5-25.meaning: Those who are pure, clear-minded, disciplined and devoted to helping all beings find God's peace.
gita-5-25.explanation: Krishna adds a social mark of the enlightened: they rejoice in the welfare of all beings. Purity, clarity and self-control combine with compassion.

keywords.meaning: delighting in the good of all

gita-5-26.translation: For those free from desire and anger, who have controlled their minds and know the Self, the peace of Brahman is close at hand on every side.
gita-5-26.meaning: For those who have mastered desire, anger and the mind, God's peace is very near.
gita-5-26.explanation: For disciplined seekers who know the Self and have overcome desire and anger, the peace of Brahman is not far away. It surrounds them in this life and beyond.

gita-5-27.translation: Shutting out external contacts, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, and evening out the in-breath and out-breath moving in the nostrils,
gita-5-27.meaning: Close off outside distractions, focus between the eyebrows and calm the breath.
gita-5-27.explanation: Krishna begins a short description of meditation that will be developed in chapter six. Shut out sense objects, rest the gaze between the eyebrows, and balance the breath. The sentence continues in the next verse.

gita-5-28.translation: with senses, mind and intellect controlled, intent on liberation, free from desire, fear and anger, such a sage is always free.
gita-5-28.meaning: A meditator who masters the senses and mind and lets go of desire, fear and anger is free.
gita-5-28.explanation: Completing the thought, the meditating sage controls senses, mind and intellect, aims only at liberation, and has given up desire, fear and anger. Such a one is already free.

gita-5-29.translation: Knowing me as the enjoyer of all sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all the worlds and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
gita-5-29.meaning: Know God as the one who receives every offering, rules all worlds and is everyone's friend. That brings peace.
gita-5-29.explanation: The chapter ends by bringing the focus to Krishna himself. He receives all offerings, is the great Lord of every world, and is the well-wisher of every creature. Knowing him this way brings peace.

gita-6-1.translation: Krishna said: One who does the work that ought to be done, without depending on its results, is a true renunciate and a true yogi, not one who merely gives up the sacred fire and ritual acts.
gita-6-1.meaning: Real renunciation is doing your duty without craving results, not just giving up rituals or work.
gita-6-1.explanation: Krishna opens the chapter on meditation by repeating his key point: outward giving up of rituals does not make someone a renunciate. The one who does what is needed without leaning on the results is both renunciate and yogi.

gita-6-2.translation: Know that what is called renunciation is yoga, Pandava. No one becomes a yogi without giving up selfish intentions.
gita-6-2.meaning: Renunciation and yoga are really the same thing: letting go of selfish plans.
gita-6-2.explanation: Renunciation and yoga share one root: giving up sankalpa, the mind's selfish scheming. Without letting go of that, no one becomes a yogi, whatever they outwardly do.

gita-6-3.translation: For the sage who wants to rise to yoga, action is the means. For the same sage, once risen to yoga, calm is the means.
gita-6-3.meaning: At first, selfless work is the path. Once you are settled, inner stillness takes you further.
gita-6-3.explanation: Krishna describes two stages. For a beginner climbing toward yoga, action is the way. Once established, peace and stillness become the way forward.

gita-6-4.translation: When one is no longer attached to sense objects or to actions, and has given up all selfish intentions, one is said to have risen to yoga.
gita-6-4.meaning: You have reached yoga when you no longer cling to pleasures or to your own activity.
gita-6-4.explanation: Krishna gives the mark of one who has climbed to yoga: no attachment to sense objects, no attachment to actions, and no selfish intentions left.

gita-6-6.translation: For one who has conquered the self by the Self, the Self is a friend. But for one who has not, the Self acts like an enemy.
gita-6-6.meaning: Your own mind can be your best friend or your worst enemy, depending on whether you master it.
gita-6-6.explanation: Following the call to lift oneself by oneself, Krishna explains: when the lower self is mastered by the higher, the self becomes a friend. Left untamed, it behaves like a hostile enemy.

gita-6-7.translation: The Supreme Self of one who has mastered himself and is at peace remains steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
gita-6-7.meaning: A self-controlled, peaceful person stays balanced through heat and cold, joy and pain, praise and insult.
gita-6-7.explanation: One who has conquered himself and found peace rests in the Supreme Self. Opposites like heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honour and insult no longer disturb that inner centre.

gita-6-8.translation: The yogi content with knowledge and wisdom, unshaken, master of the senses, to whom a clod of earth, a stone and gold are the same, is called steady in yoga.
gita-6-8.meaning: A true yogi is satisfied with wisdom and sees dirt, stone and gold as equal.
gita-6-8.explanation: Krishna describes a yogi who is fulfilled by knowledge and direct experience, unmoved like a mountain peak, in control of the senses. For such a one, earth, stone and gold have equal value.

gita-6-9.translation: One who looks equally on well-wishers, friends and enemies, the indifferent and the neutral, the hateful and relatives, the good and the wicked, stands out.
gita-6-9.meaning: The best people treat friends, enemies, strangers and family, good and bad, with the same fairness.
gita-6-9.explanation: This verse extends equality to people. The one who has the same even regard for friends and foes, strangers and kin, saints and sinners, excels among all.

gita-6-10.translation: A yogi should always practise concentration, staying alone in a quiet place, with mind and body controlled, free of expectation and possessiveness.
gita-6-10.meaning: To meditate, find a quiet place, be alone, calm the body and mind, and let go of wanting.
gita-6-10.explanation: Krishna starts his practical instructions for meditation. The practitioner should seek solitude, control mind and body, expect nothing, and own nothing in the heart.

gita-6-11.translation: In a clean place, setting up a firm seat of his own, neither too high nor too low, made of kusha grass, a deer skin and a cloth, one over the other,
gita-6-11.meaning: Choose a clean spot and a steady seat, not too high or too low.
gita-6-11.explanation: Krishna describes the seat for meditation: clean, firm, of moderate height, with layers of kusha grass, deer skin and cloth as was customary. The sentence continues into the next verse.

gita-6-12.translation: sitting there on that seat, making the mind one-pointed and controlling the activity of mind and senses, he should practise yoga to purify himself.
gita-6-12.meaning: Sit still, focus the mind on one point and practise to purify yourself.
gita-6-12.explanation: Seated, the meditator gathers the mind to a single point and restrains the restless senses. The aim of this practice is inner purification.

gita-6-13.translation: Holding body, head and neck straight and still, steady, gazing at the tip of the nose without looking around,
gita-6-13.meaning: Keep your back, neck and head straight and still, with your gaze gently fixed.
gita-6-13.explanation: Krishna describes posture: the spine, neck and head are aligned and motionless. The gaze rests near the tip of the nose rather than roaming in every direction.

gita-6-14.translation: calm and fearless, firm in the vow of celibacy, controlling the mind and thinking of me, he should sit steady in yoga, holding me as the highest goal.
gita-6-14.meaning: Sit calm and unafraid, with a disciplined life, focusing your mind on God.
gita-6-14.explanation: The meditator is peaceful, without fear and committed to a disciplined life. The mind is controlled and turned toward Krishna as the supreme goal.

gita-6-15.translation: Always uniting himself in this way, with mind controlled, the yogi reaches the peace that rests in me, the supreme freedom.
gita-6-15.meaning: Regular meditation with a disciplined mind leads to the deep peace of God.
gita-6-15.explanation: The result of steady practice is peace that abides in Krishna himself, culminating in nirvana, the supreme freedom.

gita-6-16.translation: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or too little, Arjuna, nor for one who sleeps too much or stays awake too much.
gita-6-16.meaning: Meditation needs balance: not too much or too little food, not too much or too little sleep.
gita-6-16.explanation: Krishna warns against extremes. Overeating and starving, oversleeping and staying awake too long all make yoga impossible. Balance is key.

keywords.meaning: of one who eats too much
of one who does not eat
of one who sleeps too much

gita-6-18.translation: When the disciplined mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for any desire, then one is said to be steady in yoga.
gita-6-18.meaning: You are settled in yoga when your mind rests within and no longer craves anything.
gita-6-18.explanation: When the controlled mind settles in the Self, with no craving for any object of desire, the person is called established in yoga.

gita-6-19.translation: As a lamp in a place without wind does not flicker: that is the image used for the yogi with a controlled mind, practising concentration on the Self.
gita-6-19.meaning: A calm mind in meditation is like a lamp flame that stays still where there is no wind.
gita-6-19.explanation: This is one of the Gita's best-loved images. A flame sheltered from wind burns perfectly steady. So is the mind of a yogi absorbed in the Self.

gita-6-20.translation: When the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, becomes still, and when, seeing the Self by the Self, one is content in the Self,
gita-6-20.meaning: In deep meditation the mind becomes still and you find contentment within yourself.
gita-6-20.explanation: Krishna begins a long sentence describing the state of yoga. The mind comes to rest through practice, and the meditator sees the Self by means of the Self and is satisfied there.

keywords.meaning: seeing the Self by the Self

gita-6-21.translation: when one knows that boundless joy grasped by the intellect and beyond the senses, and established there never moves from the truth,
gita-6-21.meaning: There is a joy beyond the senses, known by the deepest understanding, and once found it holds you steady.
gita-6-21.explanation: The state of yoga holds an infinite happiness that the senses cannot reach but the purified intellect can know. Established in it, one does not waver from reality.

gita-6-22.translation: having gained which one thinks there is no greater gain, and established in which one is not shaken even by great sorrow,
gita-6-22.meaning: Once you find this inner joy, nothing seems greater, and even heavy sorrow cannot shake you.
gita-6-22.explanation: Continuing the description: after attaining this state one sees no higher gain, and even a heavy grief cannot disturb one who rests in it.

gita-6-23.translation: know that as yoga: the breaking of contact with sorrow. This yoga should be practised with determination and with an undiscouraged mind.
gita-6-23.meaning: Yoga means being freed from sorrow. Practise it with resolve and do not lose heart.
gita-6-23.explanation: Krishna completes the sentence with a definition: yoga is disconnection from union with pain. It should be practised firmly, without growing discouraged.

gita-6-24.translation: Giving up completely all desires born of selfish thought, and restraining the whole group of senses on every side with the mind,
gita-6-24.meaning: Let go of all wants that come from your imagination, and gather in the senses with the mind.
gita-6-24.explanation: Krishna returns to method. Abandon every desire that arises from mental imagining, and use the mind to draw the senses back from all directions.

gita-6-25.translation: little by little one should become quiet, with the intellect held firm. Fixing the mind in the Self, one should think of nothing else.
gita-6-25.meaning: Calm the mind gradually, keep it steady, rest it within, and do not think of anything else.
gita-6-25.explanation: Progress in meditation is gradual. With a steady intellect, the mind is settled in the Self and not allowed to wander toward other thoughts.

gita-6-27.translation: Supreme happiness comes to the yogi whose mind is at peace, whose restless passion is calmed, who is free of fault and has become one with Brahman.
gita-6-27.meaning: When the mind is peaceful and restlessness has settled, the highest happiness comes.
gita-6-27.explanation: A yogi whose mind is completely calm, whose rajas, the quality of restless passion, has subsided, and who is free from faults, becomes one with Brahman and tastes supreme joy.

gita-6-28.translation: Always practising like this and free from fault, the yogi easily enjoys the endless happiness of contact with Brahman.
gita-6-28.meaning: With steady practice, the meditator comes to enjoy limitless joy in God, easily.
gita-6-28.explanation: Through continuous practice, with faults removed, the yogi enjoys the infinite bliss of touching Brahman, and it comes with ease.

gita-6-29.translation: One whose self is steady in yoga sees the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self, seeing the same everywhere.
gita-6-29.meaning: A true yogi sees themselves in everyone and everyone in themselves.
gita-6-29.explanation: This verse describes the vision that meditation brings. The yogi sees one Self in all beings and all beings resting in that Self, with equal vision everywhere.

keywords.meaning: and all beings in the Self

gita-6-30.translation: One who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me: I am never lost to that person, and that person is never lost to me.
gita-6-30.meaning: If you see God in everything and everything in God, you and God will never be apart.
gita-6-30.explanation: Krishna makes the vision personal. Whoever sees him in all things and all things in him enters a bond that is never broken from either side.

gita-6-31.translation: One who, established in oneness, worships me as present in all beings, that yogi lives in me, however he may be living.
gita-6-31.meaning: Whoever loves God present in all beings lives in God, whatever their life looks like outwardly.
gita-6-31.explanation: Krishna adds that outward circumstances do not matter. A yogi rooted in unity who honours Krishna in every being dwells in Krishna in every situation.

gita-6-32.translation: One who, comparing with himself, sees equality everywhere, Arjuna, whether in pleasure or in pain, is considered the highest yogi.
gita-6-32.meaning: The best yogi feels others' joy and pain as their own.
gita-6-32.explanation: Krishna names the highest yogi: one who uses his own experience as the measure and so feels the pleasure and pain of every being as his own. This is compassion born of oneness.

gita-6-33.translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, this yoga of evenness you have taught, I do not see how it can last, because the mind is so restless.
gita-6-33.meaning: Arjuna honestly says that a steady mind sounds wonderful, but his mind is too restless.
gita-6-33.explanation: Arjuna speaks for every meditator. The yoga of equanimity Krishna describes seems impossible to sustain, because the mind does not stay still.

gita-6-34.translation: The mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think controlling it is as hard as controlling the wind.
gita-6-34.meaning: Arjuna says controlling the mind is as hard as catching the wind.
gita-6-34.explanation: Arjuna describes the mind: restless, stormy, strong and unyielding. Holding it still seems as impossible as holding the wind.

gita-6-35.translation: Krishna said: No doubt, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it can be controlled by steady practice and by detachment.
gita-6-35.meaning: Krishna agrees the mind is hard to control, but says practice and letting go will train it.
gita-6-35.explanation: Krishna does not dismiss Arjuna's difficulty. He agrees, then gives the remedy: abhyasa, constant practice, and vairagya, dispassion. These two together tame the mind.

gita-6-36.translation: I hold that yoga is hard to reach for one without self-control. But one who is self-controlled and strives by the right means can attain it.
gita-6-36.meaning: Without discipline yoga is hard, but with effort and the right method you can reach it.
gita-6-36.explanation: Yoga is difficult for someone who makes no effort to master himself. For the disciplined who strive in the right way, it is within reach.

gita-6-37.translation: Arjuna said: What happens, Krishna, to one who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind wanders from yoga, and who fails to reach perfection?
gita-6-37.meaning: Arjuna asks what happens to someone who tries sincerely but does not succeed in this life.
gita-6-37.explanation: Arjuna raises a heartfelt worry. Suppose a person has faith but their effort is weak and their mind slips away from practice before reaching the goal. What becomes of them?

gita-6-38.translation: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a scattered cloud, without support, mighty-armed one, confused on the path to Brahman?
gita-6-38.meaning: Arjuna fears such a person loses both worldly life and spiritual progress, like a cloud breaking apart.
gita-6-38.explanation: Arjuna pictures a cloud torn from one bank of clouds and failing to reach another, dissolving in between. Has the failed seeker lost both worldly success and spiritual attainment?

gita-6-39.translation: Krishna, please remove this doubt of mine completely. No one but you can dispel it.
gita-6-39.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to clear away this doubt, since only Krishna can.
gita-6-39.explanation: Arjuna turns to Krishna as the only one able to settle this question fully.

gita-6-40.translation: Krishna said: Partha, there is no destruction for him, either in this world or the next. No one who does good, my friend, ever comes to a bad end.
gita-6-40.meaning: No sincere effort to do good is ever wasted. A person who does good never comes to ruin.
gita-6-40.explanation: Krishna's reply is gentle and firm. The seeker is not lost here or hereafter. Anyone who does good, whom Krishna calls 'dear friend', never goes to an evil fate.

gita-6-41.translation: Having reached the worlds of the righteous and lived there for countless years, the one who fell from yoga is born again in the home of the pure and prosperous.
gita-6-41.meaning: A seeker who did not finish is rewarded and then reborn into a good family to continue.
gita-6-41.explanation: Krishna explains the path of the unfinished seeker. After a long stay in heavenly worlds earned by good deeds, they are reborn in a pure and well-to-do household.

keywords.meaning: in a home of the pure and prosperous

gita-6-42.translation: Or he is born into a family of wise yogis. But such a birth is very hard to gain in this world.
gita-6-42.meaning: Or they may be born among wise spiritual people, which is a rare blessing.
gita-6-42.explanation: An even better possibility is birth into a family of wise yogis. Krishna notes such a birth is rare and precious.

gita-6-43.translation: There he regains the wisdom of his former life and strives again for perfection, joy of the Kurus.
gita-6-43.meaning: In the new life, they pick up where they left off and keep striving.
gita-6-43.explanation: Nothing is lost. In the new birth, the seeker recovers the understanding gained before and continues the work toward perfection.

gita-6-44.translation: By that former practice he is carried forward even without wanting it. Even one who merely seeks to know yoga goes beyond the ritual rules of the Vedas.
gita-6-44.meaning: Past spiritual practice naturally pulls you forward. Even the wish to learn yoga takes you far.
gita-6-44.explanation: The habits of practice from a former life draw the seeker onward almost automatically. Simply wanting to know yoga lifts one beyond mere ritual religion.

gita-6-45.translation: But the yogi who strives with effort, purified of faults and perfected over many births, then reaches the highest goal.
gita-6-45.meaning: With sincere effort over many lives, a seeker becomes pure and reaches the highest goal.
gita-6-45.explanation: Persistent effort, carried through many births and cleansing all faults, brings the yogi to perfection and the supreme goal.

gita-6-46.translation: The yogi is greater than ascetics, greater even than scholars, and greater than those devoted to ritual action. So be a yogi, Arjuna.
gita-6-46.meaning: Being a yogi is greater than harsh austerity, book learning or ritual. So become a yogi.
gita-6-46.explanation: Krishna ranks the yogi above those who practise physical austerity, those with scholarly knowledge, and those who perform rituals for reward. He urges Arjuna to become a yogi.

gita-6-47.translation: And of all yogis, the one who worships me with faith, whose inner self is absorbed in me, I consider the most closely united with me.
gita-6-47.meaning: The greatest yogi is the one who loves God with faith and keeps their heart in him.
gita-6-47.explanation: The chapter ends by pointing ahead to devotion. Among all yogis, Krishna holds highest the one who worships him with faith and whose inner self dwells in him.

keywords.meaning: with inner self absorbed in me

gita-7-1.translation: Krishna said: Partha, listen to how, with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking refuge in me, you will know me fully and without doubt.
gita-7-1.meaning: Krishna invites Arjuna to listen as he explains how to know God completely.
gita-7-1.explanation: The seventh chapter begins a new section of the Gita focused on knowing Krishna himself. With a mind fixed on him and depending on him, Arjuna will come to know him fully and without doubt.

gita-7-2.translation: I will teach you this knowledge together with direct experience, completely. Knowing it, nothing more remains to be known here.
gita-7-2.meaning: Krishna promises to share a complete wisdom, after which nothing else needs to be learned.
gita-7-2.explanation: Krishna promises both jnana, knowledge, and vijnana, realised understanding. Once this is known, there is nothing further to know in this world.

gita-7-3.translation: Among thousands of people, hardly one strives for perfection. And among those who strive and succeed, hardly one knows me as I truly am.
gita-7-3.meaning: Very few people seek God seriously, and fewer still truly come to know him.
gita-7-3.explanation: Krishna stresses how rare true knowledge is. Out of thousands, only one seeks perfection, and among such seekers, only one knows him in truth.

gita-7-4.translation: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and ego: these are the eight parts of my material nature.
gita-7-4.meaning: Everything material, including our mind and sense of 'I', is part of God's lower nature.
gita-7-4.explanation: Krishna lists the eightfold lower nature: five elements, plus mind, intellect and ego. Even the inner faculties belong to the material world.

gita-7-5.translation: This is my lower nature. But know my other, higher nature, mighty-armed one: the life principle, by which this universe is held together.
gita-7-5.meaning: Beyond matter, God has a higher nature: the living spirit that sustains all things.
gita-7-5.explanation: Beyond the eightfold material nature is Krishna's higher nature, the jiva, the conscious life principle. It upholds the whole universe.

gita-7-6.translation: Know that all beings come from these two natures. I am the origin of the whole universe and also its dissolution.
gita-7-6.meaning: Every living thing comes from matter and spirit, and God is both where everything begins and ends.
gita-7-6.explanation: Every being arises from the union of these two natures, matter and spirit. Krishna is the source from which the whole world comes and into which it dissolves.

gita-7-7.translation: There is nothing higher than me, Dhananjaya. All this is strung on me, like pearls on a thread.
gita-7-7.meaning: God is the hidden thread that holds everything together, like a string through pearls.
gita-7-7.explanation: A famous image: the world is like a necklace of pearls, and Krishna is the unseen thread running through every pearl. Nothing is higher than him.

gita-7-8.translation: I am the taste in water, son of Kunti. I am the light in the moon and the sun, the sacred syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space and the strength in human beings.
gita-7-8.meaning: God is the essence of everything: the taste of water, the light of the sun and moon, the sound in space.
gita-7-8.explanation: Krishna begins to show how he can be found in the world. He is the essential quality of each thing: water's taste, the sun and moon's light, Om in the scriptures, sound in space and manliness in people.

gita-7-9.translation: I am the pure fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in fire. I am the life in all beings and the austerity in ascetics.
gita-7-9.meaning: God is the fragrance of the earth, the heat of fire, the life in all creatures.
gita-7-9.explanation: Continuing the list: Krishna is the sweet smell of the earth, the glow of fire, the life force in every creature and the discipline of those who practise austerity.

gita-7-10.translation: Partha, know me as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the brilliance of the brilliant.
gita-7-10.meaning: God is the seed from which all life grows, and the intelligence and brilliance in gifted people.
gita-7-10.explanation: Krishna is the everlasting seed of all that exists. Whatever intelligence or brilliance appears in people is his.

gita-7-11.translation: I am the strength of the strong, free from desire and passion. In beings, I am desire that does not go against dharma, best of the Bharatas.
gita-7-11.meaning: God is pure strength without greed, and healthy desire that stays within what is right.
gita-7-11.explanation: Krishna is strength that is free of craving and attachment. He is even present in desire, so long as it is in harmony with dharma. Desire itself is not condemned.

gita-7-12.translation: Whatever states of being there are, whether pure, passionate or dull, know that they come from me. But I am not in them; they are in me.
gita-7-12.meaning: All moods and qualities come from God, but God is not limited by them.
gita-7-12.explanation: The three gunas, sattva (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (inertia), all come from Krishna. Yet he is not contained in them; they rest in him.

keywords.meaning: but I am not in them

gita-7-13.translation: The whole world is deluded by these three qualities of nature and does not recognise me, who am beyond them and unchanging.
gita-7-13.meaning: Because people are caught up in their moods and natures, they fail to see God beyond them.
gita-7-13.explanation: Living beings are bewildered by the play of the three gunas. Caught in them, they do not recognise Krishna, who stands beyond and is imperishable.

gita-7-14.translation: This divine power of illusion of mine, made of the three qualities, is hard to cross. But those who take refuge in me alone cross over it.
gita-7-14.meaning: The world's illusion is hard to escape, but those who turn to God get past it.
gita-7-14.explanation: Krishna's maya, the power that hides the truth, works through the gunas and is very hard to overcome. Only those who surrender to him pass beyond it.

gita-7-15.translation: Evil-doers, the foolish and the lowest of people do not turn to me. Their knowledge is stolen by illusion and they have taken on a demonic nature.
gita-7-15.meaning: Those who do wrong and are deeply deluded do not seek God.
gita-7-15.explanation: Krishna names those who do not turn to him: wrongdoers, the foolish and the debased. Their understanding has been robbed by maya, and they follow a demonic disposition.

gita-7-16.translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise.
gita-7-16.meaning: People come to God for four reasons: in trouble, out of curiosity, wanting help, or out of wisdom.
gita-7-16.explanation: Krishna describes four types of virtuous devotees: those in suffering, those who wish to know, those seeking some benefit, and those who already have wisdom.

gita-7-17.translation: Of these, the wise one, always steady and devoted to the One alone, is the best. I am very dear to the wise, and the wise is dear to me.
gita-7-17.meaning: Of the four, the wise devotee who loves God alone is the best, and God loves them dearly.
gita-7-17.explanation: Among the four, the wise devotee stands out, always united with Krishna and devoted to him alone. Their love is mutual.

gita-7-18.translation: All of them are noble, but I consider the wise one to be my very self. With mind steady, he holds to me alone as the highest goal.
gita-7-18.meaning: All devotees are good, but the wise one is so close to God that he is like God's own self.
gita-7-18.explanation: Krishna affirms that every sincere devotee is noble, but the wise one is so united with him that Krishna sees him as his own Self.

gita-7-19.translation: At the end of many births, the wise one takes refuge in me, knowing 'Vasudeva is everything.' Such a great soul is very rare.
gita-7-19.meaning: After many lives, the wise realise 'God is everything' and surrender to him. Such people are rare.
gita-7-19.explanation: The vision that 'Vasudeva (Krishna) is all' comes only after many lifetimes of growth. One who reaches it is a mahatma, a great soul, and very hard to find.

keywords.meaning: at the end of many births

gita-7-20.translation: Those whose understanding has been carried off by various desires turn to other gods, following particular rites, led by their own natures.
gita-7-20.meaning: When desires cloud people's understanding, they worship other gods for what they want.
gita-7-20.explanation: People driven by specific wants approach other deities, following particular rules of worship. Their own nature leads them to this.

gita-7-21.translation: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that person's faith firm in that very form.
gita-7-21.meaning: Whatever form of God someone worships with faith, God strengthens their faith in it.
gita-7-21.explanation: Krishna shows great generosity. Whatever deity someone worships with sincere faith, Krishna himself strengthens that faith.

gita-7-22.translation: Endowed with that faith, he worships that form and obtains his desires from it, though in truth it is I alone who grant them.
gita-7-22.meaning: Even when people pray to other gods, it is really the one God who answers.
gita-7-22.explanation: Filled with that faith, the devotee worships and receives his wishes. But the benefits actually come from Krishna, who works through every form.

gita-7-23.translation: But the fruit gained by those of small understanding is limited. Those who worship the gods go to the gods; my devotees come to me.
gita-7-23.meaning: Praying for limited things brings limited results. Loving God himself brings you to God.
gita-7-23.explanation: Krishna contrasts outcomes. Rewards from worshipping lesser gods end. Those who worship the gods reach the gods, but Krishna's devotees reach Krishna himself, the lasting goal.

gita-7-24.translation: The unwise think of me, the unmanifest, as having taken a manifest form. They do not know my higher nature, unchanging and supreme.
gita-7-24.meaning: People who see Krishna only as a man miss his true, limitless nature.
gita-7-24.explanation: The unwise think Krishna is merely a person who came into being. They do not know his supreme nature, which is unmanifest, imperishable and highest of all.

gita-7-25.translation: I am not revealed to everyone, being veiled by my own power of illusion. This deluded world does not know me, the unborn and unchanging.
gita-7-25.meaning: God hides himself behind his own power, so the confused world does not recognise him.
gita-7-25.explanation: Krishna's yogamaya, his veiling power, keeps him hidden. The deluded world fails to see him as unborn and imperishable.

gita-7-26.translation: I know all beings of the past, the present and the future, Arjuna, but no one knows me.
gita-7-26.meaning: God knows everyone across all time, but no one fully knows God.
gita-7-26.explanation: Krishna's knowledge covers every being in past, present and future, yet no being fully knows him.

gita-7-27.translation: All beings, from birth, fall into delusion, Bharata, through the pairs of opposites that arise from desire and aversion, scorcher of foes.
gita-7-27.meaning: From birth, likes and dislikes confuse us and hide the truth.
gita-7-27.explanation: Desire and dislike create opposites such as pleasure and pain. Caught in these from the moment of birth, all beings are deluded.

gita-7-28.translation: But those of good deeds, whose wrongdoing has come to an end, are freed from the delusion of opposites and worship me with firm resolve.
gita-7-28.meaning: People who live well and leave wrongdoing behind become free of confusion and worship God steadily.
gita-7-28.explanation: When wrongdoing ends through good actions, people are released from the confusion of opposites. They then worship Krishna with unshakeable commitment.

keywords.meaning: freed from the delusion of opposites

gita-7-29.translation: Those who take refuge in me and strive for freedom from old age and death come to know Brahman, the whole of the Self and all about action.
gita-7-29.meaning: Those who turn to God to escape ageing and death come to know the Supreme, the Self and the nature of action.
gita-7-29.explanation: Seekers who depend on Krishna and work for release from ageing and death come to know Brahman, the inner Self in full and the meaning of karma.

keywords.meaning: for freedom from age and death

gita-7-30.translation: Those who know me together with the material realm, the divine realm and sacrifice, with steady minds, know me even at the time of death.
gita-7-30.meaning: Those who see God in matter, in the divine and in worship will remember him even at the moment of death.
gita-7-30.explanation: The chapter closes with terms that Arjuna will ask about in chapter eight: adhibhuta, adhidaiva and adhiyajna. Those who know Krishna in all of these, with steady minds, know him even at the hour of death.

gita-8-1.translation: Arjuna said: What is Brahman? What is the Self? What is action, highest of beings? What is called the material realm, and what is called the divine realm?
gita-8-1.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the special terms he used at the end of the last chapter.
gita-8-1.explanation: At the end of chapter seven Krishna used several technical terms. Arjuna now asks him to define them one by one: Brahman, adhyatma, karma, adhibhuta and adhidaiva.

gita-8-2.translation: What is the realm of sacrifice, and how does it dwell in this body, Krishna? And how are you to be known at the time of death by those who are self-controlled?
gita-8-2.meaning: Arjuna also asks how God is present in the body and how one can remember him at death.
gita-8-2.explanation: Arjuna completes his questions: what is adhiyajna, how does it live in the body, and how can a disciplined person know Krishna at the moment of death?

gita-8-3.translation: Krishna said: Brahman is the imperishable, the supreme. Its own nature is called the Self. The creative force that brings beings into existence is called action.
gita-8-3.meaning: Brahman is the eternal reality. Our true nature is the Self. Action is the force that creates life.
gita-8-3.explanation: Krishna gives definitions. Brahman is the indestructible Supreme. Adhyatma is its presence as the individual's own nature. Karma is the creative outflow that brings beings into existence.

gita-8-4.translation: The material realm is perishable existence. The divine realm is the cosmic Spirit. And I myself, here in the body, am the lord of sacrifice, best of embodied beings.
gita-8-4.meaning: The physical world changes and ends. God lives within the body as the one who receives all offerings.
gita-8-4.explanation: Adhibhuta is everything that perishes, the changing world. Adhidaiva is the cosmic person who presides over the gods. Adhiyajna is Krishna himself dwelling in every body as the recipient of sacrifice.

gita-8-5.translation: Whoever, at the time of death, leaves the body remembering me alone, attains my being. There is no doubt about this.
gita-8-5.meaning: If you think of God at the moment of death, you go to God.
gita-8-5.explanation: Krishna answers the question about death. One who remembers him alone at the last moment goes to his state of being. He states this without any doubt.

keywords.meaning: at the time of the end

gita-8-6.translation: Whatever state of being one remembers when finally leaving the body, son of Kunti, to that state one goes, having always been absorbed in it.
gita-8-6.meaning: What you think about at death depends on what you have dwelt on all your life, and it shapes what comes next.
gita-8-6.explanation: This is a general law. The thought at the end leads to its corresponding state. But that last thought is shaped by what one has habitually dwelt on throughout life.

gita-8-7.translation: Therefore at all times remember me and fight. With mind and intellect offered to me, you will surely come to me.
gita-8-7.meaning: Keep God in mind at all times while doing your duty. Then you will reach him.
gita-8-7.explanation: Krishna draws the practical lesson. Since the last thought follows lifelong habit, Arjuna should remember Krishna always, and still do his duty. Devotion and action go together.

gita-8-8.translation: With a mind trained by constant practice and not wandering to anything else, meditating on the supreme divine Person, Partha, one reaches him.
gita-8-8.meaning: Steady practice that keeps the mind on God leads you to God.
gita-8-8.explanation: A mind disciplined by regular practice does not drift away. Meditating continually on the supreme divine Person, one reaches him.

keywords.meaning: trained by the yoga of practice

gita-8-9.translation: One who meditates on the all-knowing, the ancient, the ruler, smaller than the smallest, the support of all, whose form is beyond thought, radiant like the sun beyond darkness,
gita-8-9.meaning: Krishna describes the Supreme: ancient, all-knowing, tiny yet supporting everything, bright as the sun.
gita-8-9.explanation: Krishna describes the one to meditate on: the wise and ancient ruler, subtler than the subtlest, who supports everything, has an unimaginable form and shines like the sun beyond all darkness. The sentence continues into the next verse.

gita-8-10.translation: at the time of death, with a steady mind, full of devotion and by the strength of yoga, drawing the life-breath between the eyebrows, reaches that supreme divine Person.
gita-8-10.meaning: At death, a devoted and disciplined person who focuses inward reaches God.
gita-8-10.explanation: Completing the sentence: at the moment of death, with a firm mind, devotion and yogic power, the life-breath is gathered between the eyebrows and the meditator reaches the supreme Person.

gita-8-11.translation: I will briefly tell you of that state which the knowers of the Veda call imperishable, which ascetics free from passion enter, and for whose sake people live a life of celibacy.
gita-8-11.meaning: Krishna promises to explain briefly the eternal goal sought by sages and seekers.
gita-8-11.explanation: Krishna introduces the goal described in the Vedas as imperishable, reached by passionless ascetics, and sought through a disciplined, celibate life. He will now explain it briefly.

gita-8-12.translation: Closing all the gates of the body, holding the mind in the heart, placing the life-breath in the head, established in yogic concentration,
gita-8-12.meaning: At death, the meditator closes off the senses, centres the mind in the heart and lifts the breath upward.
gita-8-12.explanation: Krishna describes the yogic way of leaving the body: the sense gates are closed, the mind rests in the heart, and the vital breath is drawn up into the head. The sentence continues.

keywords.meaning: holding the mind in the heart

gita-8-13.translation: chanting Om, the single syllable that is Brahman, and remembering me, one who leaves the body in this way reaches the supreme goal.
gita-8-13.meaning: Chanting Om and remembering God as one dies leads to the highest goal.
gita-8-13.explanation: The practice concludes with chanting Om, the one-syllable sound of Brahman, while remembering Krishna. Leaving the body thus, one attains the highest destination.

gita-8-14.translation: For the yogi who always remembers me with undivided mind, I am easy to reach, Partha, for one who is constantly united with me.
gita-8-14.meaning: God is easy to reach for anyone who remembers him constantly with their whole heart.
gita-8-14.explanation: After describing a demanding yogic method, Krishna offers a simpler way. Whoever remembers him always with single-minded devotion finds him easily.

gita-8-15.translation: Having reached me, these great souls do not return to rebirth, which is the home of sorrow and does not last. They have reached the highest perfection.
gita-8-15.meaning: Those who reach God are not born again into a world of suffering.
gita-8-15.explanation: Great souls who reach Krishna do not come back to rebirth, which Krishna calls a temporary place of pain. They have attained the supreme perfection.

gita-8-16.translation: All the worlds, up to the world of Brahma, are places of return, Arjuna. But one who reaches me, son of Kunti, is not born again.
gita-8-16.meaning: Even the highest heavens are temporary. Only reaching God ends the cycle of birth.
gita-8-16.explanation: Even the realm of Brahma, the creator, is subject to return. Every world within creation is temporary. Only by reaching Krishna does rebirth end.

keywords.meaning: up to the world of Brahma

gita-8-17.translation: Those who know that a day of Brahma lasts a thousand ages and that his night also lasts a thousand ages truly know day and night.
gita-8-17.meaning: The universe moves in vast cycles. A day of the creator lasts a thousand ages.
gita-8-17.explanation: Krishna describes cosmic time. One day of Brahma lasts a thousand yugas, or great ages, and so does his night. Those who understand this know the true scale of time.

gita-8-18.translation: When Brahma's day arrives, all manifest things come forth from the unmanifest. When his night arrives, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest.
gita-8-18.meaning: Creation appears at the start of each cosmic day and dissolves back at night.
gita-8-18.explanation: At the dawn of Brahma's day, all visible things emerge from the unmanifest source. When his night falls, they merge back into it.

gita-8-19.translation: This same host of beings, coming into being again and again, dissolves helplessly at the coming of night, Partha, and comes forth again at the coming of day.
gita-8-19.meaning: All beings are born and dissolve again and again, carried by the cycles of time.
gita-8-19.explanation: The same multitude of beings is born and dissolved repeatedly, without control over the process, following the cosmic rhythm of day and night.

keywords.meaning: coming into being again and again

gita-8-20.translation: But beyond this unmanifest there is another, eternal unmanifest reality, which does not perish when all beings perish.
gita-8-20.meaning: Beyond the cycles of creation is an eternal reality that never ends.
gita-8-20.explanation: Beyond the unmanifest source from which the world comes and goes, there is a higher unmanifest existence. It is eternal and does not perish even when all beings are destroyed.

gita-8-21.translation: This unmanifest is called the imperishable. It is said to be the highest goal. Those who reach it do not return. That is my supreme home.
gita-8-21.meaning: That eternal reality is God's own home. Whoever reaches it does not come back.
gita-8-21.explanation: This higher unmanifest is the akshara, the imperishable, the supreme goal. Reaching it means no return to rebirth. Krishna calls it his highest abode.

gita-8-22.translation: That supreme Person, Partha, in whom all beings dwell and by whom all this is pervaded, can be reached by undivided devotion.
gita-8-22.meaning: The God who holds and fills everything can be reached through wholehearted love.
gita-8-22.explanation: The supreme Person contains all beings and pervades the whole world, yet can be reached by ananya bhakti, devotion directed to him alone.

gita-8-23.translation: Now I will tell you, best of the Bharatas, the times at which yogis departing this life do not return, and the times at which they return.
gita-8-23.meaning: Krishna will explain the two paths taken by souls after death.
gita-8-23.explanation: Krishna introduces a traditional teaching on the two paths souls take after death: one leading to no return and one leading back to rebirth.

gita-8-24.translation: Fire, light, day, the bright half of the month, the six months of the sun's northern course: those who know Brahman and depart by this path go to Brahman.
gita-8-24.meaning: The path of light leads the knowers of God to God.
gita-8-24.explanation: This is the path of light, described through symbols of brightness: fire, light, daytime, the waxing moon and the sun's northward journey. Knowers of Brahman travel it to Brahman.

gita-8-25.translation: Smoke, night, the dark half of the month, the six months of the sun's southern course: the yogi who goes by this path reaches the light of the moon and returns.
gita-8-25.meaning: The path of darkness leads to a temporary heaven and then back to rebirth.
gita-8-25.explanation: The other path is described with symbols of darkness: smoke, night, the waning moon and the sun's southward journey. One who goes this way reaches the lunar world and later returns.

gita-8-26.translation: These two paths, the bright and the dark, are considered the world's eternal paths. By one, a person goes and does not return. By the other, he returns again.
gita-8-26.meaning: There are two paths: one of light that frees you, and one of darkness that brings you back.
gita-8-26.explanation: Krishna summarises. The paths of light and darkness are eternal. One leads to freedom, the other to return.

gita-8-27.translation: Knowing these paths, Partha, a yogi is never confused. Therefore, Arjuna, be steady in yoga at all times.
gita-8-27.meaning: Knowing these two paths, a yogi is not confused. So stay steady in practice always.
gita-8-27.explanation: The point of this teaching is not anxiety about timing but steadiness. A yogi who understands these paths is not bewildered, and so Arjuna should remain grounded in yoga at all times.

gita-8-28.translation: Whatever merit is promised for studying the Vedas, for sacrifice, austerity and charity, the yogi who knows this goes beyond it all and reaches the supreme, original home.
gita-8-28.meaning: The yogi who understands this goes beyond every reward from ritual and good works, and reaches the highest home.
gita-8-28.explanation: The chapter ends by placing this knowledge above every reward promised for scripture study, ritual, austerity and giving. The yogi who understands it passes beyond them all to the supreme and original abode.

gita-9-1.translation: Krishna said: To you, who do not find fault, I will now reveal this deepest secret, knowledge together with realisation. Knowing it, you will be freed from all harm.
gita-9-1.meaning: Because Arjuna is open and not critical, Krishna will share his most secret teaching.
gita-9-1.explanation: Krishna begins the ninth chapter, often called the royal secret. He shares it with Arjuna because Arjuna listens without envy or fault-finding. This knowledge, joined with direct experience, frees one from evil.

keywords.meaning: you will be freed from harm

gita-9-2.translation: This is the king of knowledge, the king of secrets, the supreme purifier. It is known by direct experience, in harmony with dharma, very easy to practise and everlasting.
gita-9-2.meaning: This teaching is the best of all knowledge: purifying, clear to experience, easy to follow and eternal.
gita-9-2.explanation: Krishna praises the knowledge he is about to give. It is royal among sciences and secrets, the highest purifier, directly experienced, in line with dharma, joyful to practise and imperishable.

gita-9-3.translation: People who have no faith in this dharma, scorcher of foes, do not reach me. They return to the path of the world of death.
gita-9-3.meaning: Without faith in this teaching, people keep going around in the cycle of birth and death.
gita-9-3.explanation: Those who lack faith in this path do not reach Krishna. Instead they come back again and again to the cycle of mortal life.

keywords.meaning: on the path of the world of death

gita-9-4.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by me in my unmanifest form. All beings rest in me, but I do not rest in them.
gita-9-4.meaning: God fills the whole universe invisibly. Everything rests in God, but God is not limited by anything.
gita-9-4.explanation: Krishna is present throughout the universe in an invisible form. All beings depend on him, but he does not depend on them.

keywords.meaning: but I am not in them

gita-9-5.translation: And yet beings do not rest in me. See my divine power! I support all beings and bring them into existence, yet my self does not dwell in them.
gita-9-5.meaning: God holds everything, yet stays untouched. This mystery shows his divine power.
gita-9-5.explanation: Krishna deepens the paradox. In another sense, beings do not even rest in him, because he is not affected by them. He sustains and creates all beings but is not bound up with them. This is his yoga aishvaram, his divine mystery.

gita-9-6.translation: Just as the mighty wind, moving everywhere, always remains in space, know that in the same way all beings remain in me.
gita-9-6.meaning: All beings live in God the way wind moves within the sky, without disturbing it.
gita-9-6.explanation: Krishna gives an image. The wind roams everywhere, yet it always moves within space, and space is not disturbed. In the same way, all beings move within Krishna.

gita-9-7.translation: At the end of a cosmic age, son of Kunti, all beings return to my nature. At the beginning of the next age, I send them forth again.
gita-9-7.meaning: At the end of each cosmic cycle, all beings return to God, and he brings them out again at the start of the next.
gita-9-7.explanation: Creation runs in cycles. At the close of a kalpa, a cosmic age, all beings merge into Krishna's nature. At the start of the next, he releases them again.

keywords.meaning: at the end of an age
at the start of an age

gita-9-8.translation: Controlling my own nature, I send forth again and again this whole multitude of beings, who are helpless under the power of nature.
gita-9-8.meaning: God uses his own nature to create the world again and again, while beings are carried along by nature's laws.
gita-9-8.explanation: Krishna works through his own prakriti, nature, to release the multitude of beings repeatedly. The beings themselves are powerless, governed by nature.

gita-9-9.translation: These actions do not bind me, Dhananjaya, for I sit as one indifferent, unattached to these actions.
gita-9-9.meaning: God creates and dissolves the world but is not bound by it, because he is not attached.
gita-9-9.explanation: Even the vast work of creation does not bind Krishna. He remains like a neutral onlooker, unattached to what he does. This mirrors the teaching on selfless action.

gita-9-10.translation: Under my supervision, nature produces all that moves and does not move. Because of this, son of Kunti, the world goes round.
gita-9-10.meaning: Nature creates everything under God's watch, and that is what keeps the world turning.
gita-9-10.explanation: Krishna presides; nature does the producing. Under his oversight, prakriti brings forth all moving and unmoving beings, and this is why the world keeps revolving.

gita-9-11.translation: Fools disregard me when I take a human form, not knowing my higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.
gita-9-11.meaning: Many people see Krishna only as a man and miss that he is the Lord of all.
gita-9-11.explanation: Because Krishna appears in a human body, the deluded overlook him. They do not see his supreme nature as the great Lord of beings.

gita-9-12.translation: Their hopes are in vain, their actions are in vain, their knowledge is in vain. Lacking discernment, they cling to a deceptive nature that is fierce and demonic.
gita-9-12.meaning: People who ignore God end up with empty hopes, wasted effort and confused minds.
gita-9-12.explanation: Those who disregard Krishna find their hopes, deeds and knowledge come to nothing. Without discernment, they take on a deluded nature that is cruel and demonic.

gita-9-13.translation: But great souls, Partha, who take shelter in the divine nature, worship me with undivided minds, knowing me as the unchanging source of all beings.
gita-9-13.meaning: Great souls with a divine nature worship God wholeheartedly, knowing he is the source of everything.
gita-9-13.explanation: In contrast, mahatmas, great souls, live by the divine nature. Knowing Krishna as the imperishable source of beings, they worship him with minds turned to nothing else.

gita-9-14.translation: Always singing my praises, striving with firm resolve, bowing down to me with devotion, they worship me, ever united with me.
gita-9-14.meaning: Devotees sing God's praise, strive with dedication, bow in love and stay close to him always.
gita-9-14.explanation: Krishna describes how great souls worship: by constantly praising him, by earnest effort and firm vows, by bowing with love, always united with him.

gita-9-15.translation: Others, offering the sacrifice of knowledge, worship me as the One, as distinct, and as the many, facing in every direction.
gita-9-15.meaning: Some worship God through wisdom, seeing him as one, as separate, or as present in all forms.
gita-9-15.explanation: Some devotees worship through the sacrifice of knowledge. They approach Krishna as the one reality, as distinct from them, or as present in countless forms facing everywhere.

gita-9-16.translation: I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the healing herb. I am the sacred chant, I am the ghee, I am the fire and I am the act of offering.
gita-9-16.meaning: God is every part of worship: the ritual, the offering, the chant, the fire.
gita-9-16.explanation: Krishna identifies himself with every element of Vedic worship. The ritual, the sacrifice, the offering to forebears, the herb, the mantra, the butter, the fire and the oblation are all him.

gita-9-17.translation: I am the father of this world, the mother, the sustainer and the grandfather. I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.
gita-9-17.meaning: God is our father, mother and support, and the wisdom of all scripture.
gita-9-17.explanation: Krishna names himself as the parent and guardian of the world, its father, mother, supporter and grandsire. He is the object of knowledge, the purifier, Om, and the three Vedas.

gita-9-18.translation: I am the goal, the support, the lord, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend. I am the origin and the dissolution, the foundation, the treasure-house and the imperishable seed.
gita-9-18.meaning: God is our goal, support, witness, home, refuge and best friend, the beginning and end of all.
gita-9-18.explanation: In one of the Gita's most loved verses, Krishna lists the ways he relates to every being: goal, sustainer, master, witness, dwelling, shelter and friend; source and end; ground, storehouse and eternal seed.
