gita-9-19.translation: I give heat. I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and also death, being and non-being, Arjuna.
gita-9-19.meaning: God controls the sun and the rain, and is both life and death, what is and what is not.
gita-9-19.explanation: Krishna is the power behind nature: the sun's heat, the withholding and release of rain. He is both deathlessness and death, the real and the unreal.

gita-9-20.translation: Those who know the three Vedas, who drink the soma and are purified of sin, worship me with sacrifices and pray for the way to heaven. They reach the holy world of Indra and enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods in heaven.
gita-9-20.meaning: People who perform rituals for heaven do reach heaven and enjoy its pleasures.
gita-9-20.explanation: Krishna describes ritualists who master the three Vedas, perform soma sacrifices and seek heaven. Through him, they reach Indra's realm and enjoy the delights of the gods.

gita-9-21.translation: Having enjoyed that vast heaven, when their merit is used up they come back to the world of mortals. Following the rules of the three Vedas and desiring pleasures, they keep coming and going.
gita-9-21.meaning: Heaven earned by good deeds runs out, and then people are born again. Chasing pleasures keeps the cycle going.
gita-9-21.explanation: Heaven is temporary. When the merit that earned it is exhausted, the soul returns to mortal life. Those who perform ritual for pleasure stay caught in coming and going.

gita-9-23.translation: Even devotees of other gods who worship with faith are really worshipping me, son of Kunti, though not in the proper way.
gita-9-23.meaning: People who sincerely worship other gods are really worshipping the one God, just indirectly.
gita-9-23.explanation: Krishna is generous toward other forms of worship. Those who sincerely worship other gods are in fact worshipping him, though not according to the deepest understanding.

gita-9-24.translation: For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices. But they do not know me as I truly am, and so they fall back.
gita-9-24.meaning: God receives every offering, but those who do not recognise him keep returning to the cycle.
gita-9-24.explanation: Krishna is the true recipient and master of every sacrifice. Those who do not recognise this receive limited fruits and fall back into rebirth.

gita-9-25.translation: Those devoted to the gods go to the gods. Those devoted to the ancestors go to the ancestors. Those who worship spirits go to the spirits. But those who worship me come to me.
gita-9-25.meaning: You become like what you worship. Worship God, and you go to God.
gita-9-25.explanation: Each type of worship leads to its own destination. Those who worship gods, ancestors or spirits reach them. Krishna's worshippers reach him.

gita-9-27.translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, whatever discipline you practise, son of Kunti, do it as an offering to me.
gita-9-27.meaning: Turn everything you do, from eating to giving to work, into an offering to God.
gita-9-27.explanation: After saying he accepts even a leaf or flower offered with love, Krishna widens the idea. All of life, from eating to giving to practising discipline, can be offered to him. Daily life becomes worship.

gita-9-28.translation: In this way you will be freed from the bonds of action and their good and bad results. With your mind steady in the yoga of renunciation, you will be free and will come to me.
gita-9-28.meaning: When you offer all your actions to God, you are freed from their consequences and reach him.
gita-9-28.explanation: Offering all actions to Krishna releases one from the binding results, both pleasant and unpleasant. Through this yoga of surrender, one is liberated and reaches him.

keywords.meaning: steady in the yoga of renunciation

gita-9-29.translation: I am the same toward all beings. No one is hateful to me and no one is dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.
gita-9-29.meaning: God has no favourites, but those who love him live in him, and he lives in them.
gita-9-29.explanation: Krishna treats every being equally, hating none and favouring none. Yet those who turn to him in love enter into a mutual indwelling: they are in him, and he is in them.

gita-9-30.translation: Even if someone with very bad conduct worships me with undivided devotion, that person should be regarded as good, for they have resolved rightly.
gita-9-30.meaning: Even a person who has done great wrong becomes good once they turn wholeheartedly to God.
gita-9-30.explanation: This is a verse of great mercy. If even a person of very bad conduct turns to Krishna with complete devotion, he should be counted as a saint, because his resolve is now right.

gita-9-31.translation: Quickly such a person becomes righteous and reaches lasting peace. Son of Kunti, declare it boldly: my devotee never perishes.
gita-9-31.meaning: A person who turns to God soon becomes good and finds peace. God's devotee is never lost.
gita-9-31.explanation: Change follows quickly. The one who turns to Krishna becomes virtuous and attains everlasting peace. Krishna asks Arjuna to proclaim that his devotee is never lost.

gita-9-32.translation: Those who take refuge in me, Partha, even those born in lowly families, women, vaishyas and shudras, also reach the highest goal.
gita-9-32.meaning: Anyone at all who turns to God reaches the highest goal, regardless of birth, gender or status.
gita-9-32.explanation: Krishna lists groups that the society of his time often excluded from spiritual learning, and says all of them reach the supreme goal by taking refuge in him. The verse reflects the social attitudes of its age, but its point is that devotion is open to everyone.

gita-9-33.translation: How much more, then, holy brahmins and devoted royal sages. Since you have come into this passing and joyless world, worship me.
gita-9-33.meaning: If even the most overlooked reach God, surely the devoted will. Life is short, so turn to God now.
gita-9-33.explanation: If devotion carries everyone to the goal, it certainly carries sages and kings. Because this world is temporary and without lasting happiness, Krishna urges Arjuna to worship him.

gita-9-34.translation: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, offer to me, bow to me. Uniting yourself with me and holding me as your goal, you will come to me.
gita-9-34.meaning: Think of God, love God, offer to God and bow to God. Then you will reach him.
gita-9-34.explanation: The chapter ends with a simple, complete path of devotion: keep the mind on Krishna, love him, worship him and bow to him. Making him the goal, one surely reaches him.

gita-10-1.translation: Krishna said: Listen again, mighty-armed one, to my supreme word, which I will tell you out of a wish for your good, because you are dear to me.
gita-10-1.meaning: Because Arjuna is dear to him, Krishna will share more of his highest teaching.
gita-10-1.explanation: The tenth chapter opens with affection. Krishna continues to teach because he cares for Arjuna's wellbeing and loves him.

gita-10-2.translation: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know my origin, for I am the source of the gods and the great sages in every way.
gita-10-2.meaning: Even gods and sages cannot know where God comes from, because he came before them all.
gita-10-2.explanation: No god or great seer knows how Krishna came to be, because he is their source. What comes after cannot fully grasp what came first.

gita-10-3.translation: One who knows me as unborn, without beginning, and the great Lord of the worlds is free from delusion among mortals and released from all sins.
gita-10-3.meaning: Knowing God as unborn, beginningless and Lord of all frees you from confusion and wrongdoing.
gita-10-3.explanation: To know Krishna as unborn, beginningless and the supreme Lord of all worlds is liberating. Such a person is undeluded and freed from every sin.

gita-10-4.translation: Intelligence, knowledge, freedom from confusion, patience, truth, self-control, calm, pleasure and pain, birth and death, fear and fearlessness,
gita-10-4.meaning: All our inner qualities, good and difficult, come from God.
gita-10-4.explanation: Krishna begins listing the qualities and states found in living beings: intelligence, knowledge, clarity, forgiveness, truthfulness, restraint, calm, pleasure and pain, becoming and ceasing, fear and courage. The list continues in the next verse.

gita-10-5.translation: non-violence, evenness, contentment, austerity, generosity, fame and disgrace: these different states of beings come from me alone.
gita-10-5.meaning: Kindness, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, honour and dishonour all arise from God.
gita-10-5.explanation: The list continues: non-harming, equanimity, contentment, discipline, charity, fame and infamy. All these states in beings come from Krishna alone.

gita-10-6.translation: The seven great sages, the four ancient ones before them, and the Manus were born from my mind and share my nature. From them come all the creatures of the world.
gita-10-6.meaning: The first sages and ancestors of humanity were born from God's mind.
gita-10-6.explanation: Krishna names the great ancestors: the seven great rishis, the four earlier sages (the Kumaras, by tradition), and the Manus. They arose from his mind, and all beings in the world descend from them.

gita-10-7.translation: One who truly knows this glory and power of mine is united with me in unwavering yoga. There is no doubt about this.
gita-10-7.meaning: Whoever truly understands God's greatness becomes steady and united with him.
gita-10-7.explanation: Knowing Krishna's vibhuti, his divine glory, and his yoga, his power, in truth, brings a steady and unshakeable union with him.

gita-10-8.translation: I am the source of everything; from me everything comes forth. Understanding this, the wise worship me, filled with love.
gita-10-8.meaning: God is the origin of all things. The wise who see this love and worship him.
gita-10-8.explanation: This begins four verses often called the heart of the Gita. Krishna is the source and the moving force of all. The wise who grasp this worship him with deep feeling.

keywords.meaning: I am the source of all

gita-10-9.translation: With their minds on me, their lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and full of joy.
gita-10-9.meaning: Devotees think of God, give their lives to him, talk about him together and are happy.
gita-10-9.explanation: Krishna describes devotees in community: their thoughts and lives are centred on him, they inspire one another, they constantly speak of him, and they find contentment and delight.

gita-10-10.translation: To those who are always devoted and worship me with love, I give the understanding by which they come to me.
gita-10-10.meaning: God gives his loving devotees the wisdom they need to reach him.
gita-10-10.explanation: Krishna responds to love. To those who are steadily devoted and worship him with joy, he gives buddhi-yoga, the yoga of understanding, which brings them to him.

gita-10-11.translation: Out of compassion for them, I, dwelling in their hearts, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
gita-10-11.meaning: Out of kindness, God lives in our hearts and lights a lamp of wisdom that drives away ignorance.
gita-10-11.explanation: Krishna explains how he gives understanding. Out of compassion he lives in the devotee's heart and lights the lamp of knowledge, which removes the darkness of ignorance.

gita-10-12.translation: Arjuna said: You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier, the eternal divine Person, the original God, unborn and all-pervading.
gita-10-12.meaning: Arjuna declares that Krishna is the Supreme God, eternal and everywhere.
gita-10-12.explanation: Moved by what he has heard, Arjuna praises Krishna as the highest reality, the ultimate refuge, the greatest purifier, the eternal divine being and the first God.

gita-10-13.translation: All the sages say this of you, as do the divine sage Narada, and Asita, Devala and Vyasa. And now you yourself tell me.
gita-10-13.meaning: Great sages have long said this about Krishna, and now Krishna confirms it himself.
gita-10-13.explanation: Arjuna notes that the great seers, including Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa, have all proclaimed this. Now Krishna himself says it.

gita-10-14.translation: I accept as true all that you tell me, Keshava. Lord, neither the gods nor the demons know your true manifestation.
gita-10-14.meaning: Arjuna accepts everything Krishna has said, knowing that even gods cannot fully grasp him.
gita-10-14.explanation: Arjuna affirms his faith. He believes everything Krishna says, and recognises that neither gods nor their opponents, the danavas, truly understand who Krishna is.

gita-10-15.translation: You alone know yourself by yourself, Supreme Person, source of beings, lord of beings, God of gods, master of the world.
gita-10-15.meaning: Only God can fully know himself.
gita-10-15.explanation: Arjuna addresses Krishna with many titles and admits that only Krishna knows Krishna. No one else can fully understand him.

gita-10-16.translation: Please tell me fully of your divine glories, by which you pervade these worlds and remain in them.
gita-10-16.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to describe the ways he is present throughout the world.
gita-10-16.explanation: Arjuna asks Krishna to describe completely his divine manifestations, the forms of glory through which he fills and abides in all the worlds.

gita-10-17.translation: How may I know you, Yogi, by always meditating on you? In what different forms should I think of you, Lord?
gita-10-17.meaning: Arjuna asks how to keep God in mind, and what forms to think of him in.
gita-10-17.explanation: Arjuna asks a practical question. How can he meditate on Krishna constantly? In which aspects or forms should he think of him?

keywords.meaning: you are to be thought of

gita-10-18.translation: Tell me again in detail of your power and glory, Janardana. I never tire of hearing your nectar-like words.
gita-10-18.meaning: Arjuna asks to hear more, because he never tires of Krishna's words.
gita-10-18.explanation: Arjuna requests a detailed description of Krishna's yoga and glory. Hearing Krishna's words is like drinking nectar, and he never has enough.

gita-10-19.translation: Krishna said: Very well. I will tell you of my divine glories, best of the Kurus, but only the chief ones, because there is no end to my details.
gita-10-19.meaning: Krishna agrees but says he can only name the most important, because his glory has no end.
gita-10-19.explanation: Krishna agrees and begins the list of his vibhutis, divine manifestations. He will name only the principal ones, because his manifestations are endless.

gita-10-20.translation: I am the Self, Gudakesha, seated in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all beings.
gita-10-20.meaning: God lives in every heart as the true Self, and is the start, middle and end of every life.
gita-10-20.explanation: Krishna's first and deepest manifestation is not in the outer world but within. He is the Self in every heart, and the origin, life and end of every being.

keywords.meaning: seated in the heart of all beings

gita-10-21.translation: Among the Adityas I am Vishnu. Among lights I am the radiant sun. Among the Maruts I am Marichi. Among the stars I am the moon.
gita-10-21.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. Among the sun gods he is Vishnu, among lights the sun.
gita-10-21.explanation: Krishna begins naming the best of each group. Among the twelve Adityas, the sun deities, he is Vishnu. Among lights, the sun. Among the storm gods, Marichi. Among the night lights, the moon.

gita-10-22.translation: Among the Vedas I am the Sama Veda. Among the gods I am Indra. Among the senses I am the mind. In living beings I am consciousness.
gita-10-22.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the Sama Veda of song, and the awareness in all life.
gita-10-22.explanation: Krishna is the Sama Veda, the Veda of sacred song; Indra, king of the gods; the mind, which leads the senses; and the consciousness present in all beings.

gita-10-23.translation: Among the Rudras I am Shankara. Among the yakshas and rakshasas I am Kubera, lord of wealth. Among the Vasus I am fire. Among mountains I am Meru.
gita-10-23.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is Shiva among the Rudras and Meru among mountains.
gita-10-23.explanation: Krishna is Shankara (Shiva) among the Rudras, Kubera the god of wealth among nature spirits, Agni (fire) among the Vasus, and the cosmic mountain Meru among peaks.

gita-10-24.translation: Among priests, Partha, know me to be their chief, Brihaspati. Among generals I am Skanda. Among bodies of water I am the ocean.
gita-10-24.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the chief of priests, the greatest general and the ocean.
gita-10-24.explanation: Krishna is Brihaspati, chief priest of the gods; Skanda, commander of the divine army; and the ocean among all bodies of water.

gita-10-25.translation: Among great sages I am Bhrigu. Among words I am the single syllable Om. Among offerings I am the offering of silent repetition. Among things that do not move I am the Himalaya.
gita-10-25.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is Om among sounds and the Himalaya among steady things.
gita-10-25.explanation: Krishna is Bhrigu among the great seers, Om among words, japa (quiet repetition of a sacred name) among forms of worship, and the Himalaya among immovable things.

gita-10-26.translation: Among all trees I am the sacred fig. Among divine sages I am Narada. Among the gandharvas I am Chitraratha. Among the perfected ones I am the sage Kapila.
gita-10-26.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the holy fig tree, the sage Narada and the sage Kapila.
gita-10-26.explanation: Krishna is the ashvattha, the sacred fig tree; Narada among divine sages; Chitraratha among the celestial musicians; and Kapila, the founder of Sankhya, among perfected beings.

gita-10-27.translation: Among horses know me as Ucchaihshravas, born from the nectar. Among lordly elephants I am Airavata, and among people I am the king.
gita-10-27.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the finest horse, the finest elephant and the ruler among people.
gita-10-27.explanation: Krishna is Ucchaihshravas, the divine horse that rose from the churning of the ocean of milk; Airavata, Indra's elephant; and the king among men.

gita-10-28.translation: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt. Among cows I am Kamadhenu, the wish-fulfilling cow. Among causes of birth I am Kandarpa, god of love. Among serpents I am Vasuki.
gita-10-28.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the thunderbolt, the wish-granting cow and the love that brings new life.
gita-10-28.explanation: Krishna is Indra's thunderbolt, Kamadhuk the cow that grants all wishes, Kandarpa the god of love as the force behind procreation, and Vasuki the king of serpents.

gita-10-29.translation: Among the nagas I am Ananta. Among the beings of the waters I am Varuna. Among the ancestors I am Aryaman. Among those who govern I am Yama.
gita-10-29.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is Ananta the great serpent, Varuna of the waters and Yama the lord of death.
gita-10-29.explanation: Krishna is Ananta, the endless serpent; Varuna, lord of the waters; Aryaman, chief of the ancestors; and Yama, who governs and judges after death.

gita-10-30.translation: Among the daityas I am Prahlada. Among measurers I am time. Among beasts I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda, son of Vinata.
gita-10-30.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the faithful Prahlada, time itself, the lion and Garuda.
gita-10-30.explanation: Krishna is Prahlada, the great devotee born among the daityas; time, which measures all; the lion, king of beasts; and Garuda, king of birds.

gita-10-31.translation: Among purifiers I am the wind. Among those who bear arms I am Rama. Among sea creatures I am the makara, and among rivers I am the Ganga.
gita-10-31.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the purifying wind, the hero Rama and the holy Ganga.
gita-10-31.explanation: Krishna is the wind, which cleanses; Rama, the greatest of warriors; the makara, a great water creature; and the Ganga, most sacred of rivers.

gita-10-32.translation: Of all creations I am the beginning, the end and the middle, Arjuna. Of all knowledge I am knowledge of the Self. Among those who debate I am reasoned argument.
gita-10-32.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the beginning, middle and end of creation, and the knowledge of the Self.
gita-10-32.explanation: Krishna is the origin, continuation and end of all that is created. Among sciences he is adhyatma-vidya, knowledge of the Self. In debate, he is the reasoning that seeks truth.

gita-10-33.translation: Among letters I am the letter A. Among compounds I am the paired compound. I am also unending time, and I am the sustainer whose face is everywhere.
gita-10-33.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the first letter A and unending time.
gita-10-33.explanation: Krishna is A, the first sound of the alphabet, and the dvandva, a type of grammatical compound that joins equals. He is also endless time and the one who supports all, facing every direction.

gita-10-34.translation: I am death that takes everything, and the birth of all that is to come. Among feminine qualities I am fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness and forgiveness.
gita-10-34.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is death and birth, and the qualities of fame, memory and patience.
gita-10-34.explanation: Krishna is death, which carries everything away, and the source of all future beings. He is also seven qualities named as feminine in Sanskrit: fame, fortune, fine speech, memory, intelligence, steadiness and forgiveness.

gita-10-35.translation: Among hymns I am the Brihat Saman. Among metres I am the Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha, and among seasons I am spring, the season of flowers.
gita-10-35.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is the Gayatri metre and the flowering spring.
gita-10-35.explanation: Krishna is the Brihat Saman hymn, the Gayatri metre in which the most sacred mantra is set, Margashirsha (November to December) among months, and spring among seasons.

gita-10-36.translation: I am the gambling of the cheats and the splendour of the splendid. I am victory, I am effort, and I am the goodness of the good.
gita-10-36.meaning: Even in the cleverness of a gambler, God's power is present, and he is victory and goodness itself.
gita-10-36.explanation: Krishna surprises by naming the gambling of the deceitful. Everything that is powerful, even used wrongly, draws on his energy. He is also brilliance, victory, determination and the goodness of good people.

gita-10-37.translation: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva. Among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya. Among sages I am Vyasa, and among poets I am the poet Ushanas.
gita-10-37.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is Krishna among his clan, Arjuna among the Pandavas, and Vyasa among sages.
gita-10-37.explanation: Krishna names himself among the Vrishnis, his own clan. He is Arjuna (Dhananjaya) among the Pandavas, Vyasa, author of the Mahabharata, among sages, and Ushanas, the wise Shukracharya, among poets.

gita-10-38.translation: Among those who punish I am the rod of justice. Among those who seek victory I am wise policy. Among secrets I am silence, and among the wise I am wisdom.
gita-10-38.meaning: Krishna is naming the greatest of each kind as a sign of his presence. He is justice, good strategy, silence and wisdom.
gita-10-38.explanation: Krishna is the rod of authority that maintains order, the sound policy of those seeking victory, the silence that guards secrets, and the knowledge of the knowers.

gita-10-39.translation: Whatever is the seed of all beings, that I am, Arjuna. There is nothing, moving or unmoving, that can exist without me.
gita-10-39.meaning: God is the seed of everything. Nothing at all can exist without him.
gita-10-39.explanation: Summing up, Krishna says he is the seed from which every being grows. Nothing that moves or stays still can exist apart from him.

gita-10-40.translation: There is no end to my divine glories, scorcher of foes. What I have told you is only a small sample of my vast glory.
gita-10-40.meaning: What Krishna has listed is only a small sample. His glory is endless.
gita-10-40.explanation: Krishna says his list is only illustrative. His divine manifestations have no limit, and he has given only a brief account.

gita-10-41.translation: Whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful, know that it comes from a spark of my splendour.
gita-10-41.meaning: Whenever you see something great, beautiful or powerful, know it reflects a spark of God.
gita-10-41.explanation: Krishna offers a simple rule for seeing him in the world. Wherever there is excellence, beauty, prosperity or strength, it springs from a fragment of his radiance.

keywords.meaning: born of a spark of my splendour

gita-10-42.translation: But what is the use of all these details to you, Arjuna? I stand, holding up this entire universe with just one fragment of myself.
gita-10-42.meaning: The whole universe is supported by only a tiny part of God.
gita-10-42.explanation: Krishna ends the chapter by pointing beyond the list. The whole universe is held up by just a fraction of his being. He is far greater than anything that can be named.

gita-11-1.translation: Arjuna said: Out of kindness to me you have spoken this supreme secret about the Self. Through it my confusion has gone.
gita-11-1.meaning: Arjuna thanks Krishna: his teaching has cleared Arjuna's confusion.
gita-11-1.explanation: The eleventh chapter, the vision of the cosmic form, begins with Arjuna's gratitude. Krishna's words about the Self have removed the delusion that paralysed him at the start.

gita-11-2.translation: Lotus-eyed one, I have heard from you in detail about the coming and going of beings, and also about your unending greatness.
gita-11-2.meaning: Arjuna has learned how beings are born and die, and about God's endless greatness.
gita-11-2.explanation: Arjuna summarises what he has learned: how beings arise and dissolve, and the imperishable majesty of Krishna.

gita-11-3.translation: Supreme Lord, it is just as you have described yourself. But I long to see your divine form, Supreme Person.
gita-11-3.meaning: Arjuna believes Krishna's words, but now wants to see God's divine form with his own eyes.
gita-11-3.explanation: Arjuna accepts all Krishna has said, but a deeper longing arises. He wants to see Krishna's majestic, sovereign form directly.

gita-11-4.translation: Lord, if you think it is possible for me to see it, then, Lord of Yoga, show me your eternal self.
gita-11-4.meaning: Arjuna humbly asks to see the vision, if Krishna thinks he is ready.
gita-11-4.explanation: Arjuna's request is humble. He asks only if Krishna considers him able to see it. Then he asks the Lord of Yoga to reveal his imperishable self.

gita-11-5.translation: Krishna said: Partha, behold my forms, by hundreds and thousands, divine, of many kinds, many colours and shapes.
gita-11-5.meaning: Krishna invites Arjuna to see his countless divine forms.
gita-11-5.explanation: Krishna agrees and begins to reveal his universal form: hundreds and thousands of divine forms, in every colour and shape.

gita-11-6.translation: See the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins and the Maruts. See many wonders never seen before, Bharata.
gita-11-6.meaning: Krishna shows Arjuna all the gods and many marvels never seen before.
gita-11-6.explanation: Within Krishna's form Arjuna is invited to see whole classes of Vedic gods: Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, the twin Ashvins and the storm gods. He will see wonders no one has seen.

gita-11-7.translation: Here today, Gudakesha, see the whole universe, moving and unmoving, gathered in one place in my body, and whatever else you wish to see.
gita-11-7.meaning: The entire universe can be seen inside God's body.
gita-11-7.explanation: Krishna tells Arjuna to see the entire universe, all that moves and all that is still, standing together in one place within his body.

gita-11-8.translation: But you cannot see me with these eyes of yours. I give you divine sight. Behold my divine power.
gita-11-8.meaning: Ordinary eyes cannot see this vision, so Krishna gives Arjuna divine sight.
gita-11-8.explanation: Human eyes cannot perceive the cosmic form. Krishna grants Arjuna a divya chakshu, a divine eye, so that he can see the Lord's sovereign power.

gita-11-9.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, O King, the great Lord of Yoga, Hari, revealed to Partha his supreme divine form.
gita-11-9.meaning: Sanjaya tells the blind king that Krishna then showed Arjuna his supreme form.
gita-11-9.explanation: Sanjaya, narrating to King Dhritarashtra, reports that Krishna, called Hari, the great master of yoga, revealed his supreme cosmic form to Arjuna.

gita-11-10.translation: With many mouths and eyes, with many wondrous sights, with many divine ornaments and many divine weapons raised,
gita-11-10.meaning: The form had countless faces, eyes, ornaments and raised weapons.
gita-11-10.explanation: Sanjaya begins describing the cosmic form: countless mouths and eyes, many astonishing appearances, divine jewellery and uplifted divine weapons.

gita-11-11.translation: wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, all-wonderful, radiant, endless, with faces turned in every direction.
gita-11-11.meaning: The divine form was adorned, fragrant, infinite and facing everywhere.
gita-11-11.explanation: The description continues: divine garlands, robes and perfumes. The form is full of wonder, shining, without limit, and looking out in all directions.

gita-11-12.translation: If the light of a thousand suns were to blaze all at once in the sky, it might be like the splendour of that great being.
gita-11-12.meaning: God's brilliance was like a thousand suns rising together.
gita-11-12.explanation: This is one of the most famous verses of the Gita. Sanjaya can only describe the radiance of the cosmic form by comparison: it was as if a thousand suns blazed in the sky at once.

gita-11-13.translation: There, in the body of the God of gods, the son of Pandu saw the whole universe, with its many divisions, gathered in one place.
gita-11-13.meaning: Arjuna saw the whole universe, in all its variety, inside God.
gita-11-13.explanation: Arjuna sees the entire universe, with all its varied parts, united in one place within the body of the God of gods.

keywords.meaning: in the body of the God of gods

gita-11-14.translation: Then Dhananjaya, filled with wonder, his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the Lord and spoke with joined palms.
gita-11-14.meaning: Overwhelmed with awe, Arjuna bowed with folded hands and spoke.
gita-11-14.explanation: Arjuna's response is physical: he is struck with amazement, his hair stands on end, he bows his head and folds his hands in reverence before he speaks.

gita-11-15.translation: Arjuna said: In your body, Lord, I see all the gods and all kinds of beings: Brahma the creator seated on the lotus, all the sages and the divine serpents.
gita-11-15.meaning: Arjuna sees all the gods, the creator Brahma, the sages and the serpents within God.
gita-11-15.explanation: Arjuna begins a hymn of praise. Inside Krishna's body he sees every god and every class of being, including Brahma on his lotus seat, the rishis and the celestial serpents.

gita-11-16.translation: I see you everywhere, infinite in form, with countless arms, bellies, mouths and eyes. I see no end, no middle and no beginning to you, Lord of the universe, whose form is the universe.
gita-11-16.meaning: God's form has no beginning, middle or end; it is everywhere.
gita-11-16.explanation: Arjuna sees Krishna's form spreading in every direction, with numberless arms and faces. He can find no beginning, middle or end in it. Krishna is the universe itself.

keywords.word: na antam na madhyam na punaḥ ādim

gita-11-17.translation: I see you with crown, mace and discus, a mass of light shining everywhere, hard to look at, blazing on all sides like fire and the sun, beyond measure.
gita-11-17.meaning: Krishna's form shines like fire and the sun, so bright it is hard to look at.
gita-11-17.explanation: Arjuna sees the familiar emblems of Vishnu, the crown, mace and discus, but now within a blaze of light so intense it can hardly be looked at, radiant like fire and sun and immeasurable.

gita-11-18.translation: You are the imperishable, the supreme one to be known. You are the final resting place of this universe. You are the unchanging guardian of eternal dharma. You are, I believe, the eternal Person.
gita-11-18.meaning: Arjuna recognises Krishna as the eternal one, the support of the universe and the protector of dharma.
gita-11-18.explanation: In awe, Arjuna declares who Krishna is: the imperishable reality to be known, the ultimate support of all, the protector of eternal dharma and the everlasting Person.

gita-11-19.translation: I see you without beginning, middle or end, of infinite power, with countless arms, the sun and moon as your eyes, your face a blazing fire, burning up this universe with your radiance.
gita-11-19.meaning: Krishna's power is endless; the sun and moon are his eyes, and his radiance blazes over the world.
gita-11-19.explanation: Arjuna continues: Krishna's power is infinite and his arms countless. The sun and moon are his eyes, and his mouth is like a sacrificial fire whose heat sets the universe ablaze.

gita-11-20.translation: The space between heaven and earth and all directions are filled by you alone. Seeing this wonderful and terrible form of yours, great one, the three worlds tremble.
gita-11-20.meaning: God fills all of space, and the worlds tremble at the sight of his awesome form.
gita-11-20.explanation: Krishna fills the sky, the earth and everything between, in every direction. His form is both marvellous and fearsome, and all three worlds shake at the sight.

gita-11-21.translation: Hosts of gods enter into you. Some, afraid, praise you with joined palms. Bands of great sages and perfected beings cry 'May all be well!' and praise you with many hymns.
gita-11-21.meaning: The gods enter God; some pray in fear, while sages sing his praises.
gita-11-21.explanation: Arjuna sees the gods streaming into Krishna. Some pray in fear with folded hands. The great seers and perfected ones call out blessings and sing hymns of praise.

gita-11-22.translation: The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, the Ashvins, Maruts and ancestors, and hosts of gandharvas, yakshas, asuras and perfected beings all gaze at you in amazement.
gita-11-22.meaning: Every kind of divine and heavenly being looks on God in amazement.
gita-11-22.explanation: Arjuna lists the many groups of heavenly beings, from gods to celestial musicians, nature spirits and demons. All stare at Krishna, astonished.

gita-11-23.translation: Seeing your great form, with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs and feet, many bellies and many terrible tusks, mighty-armed one, the worlds are terrified, and so am I.
gita-11-23.meaning: The vast form with its fearsome teeth frightens all the worlds, and Arjuna too.
gita-11-23.explanation: Now Arjuna's wonder turns to fear. The immense form, with endless limbs and dreadful teeth, terrifies the worlds and Arjuna himself.

gita-11-24.translation: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing in many colours, with mouths wide open and huge flaming eyes, my inner self trembles, Vishnu, and I find no courage and no peace.
gita-11-24.meaning: Seeing this blazing, vast form, Arjuna loses his courage and his calm.
gita-11-24.explanation: Krishna's form reaches the heavens and blazes in many colours, with gaping mouths and fiery eyes. Arjuna's heart shakes and he loses both steadiness and peace.

gita-11-25.translation: Seeing your mouths with their terrible tusks, like the fire at the end of time, I lose my sense of direction and find no shelter. Have mercy, Lord of gods, refuge of the world.
gita-11-25.meaning: Terrified, Arjuna feels lost and begs God for mercy.
gita-11-25.explanation: The tusked mouths look like the fire that consumes the world at the end of time. Arjuna loses all bearings and cries out for mercy to the refuge of the universe.

keywords.meaning: fire of the end of time
I do not know the directions

gita-11-26.translation: All these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with the hosts of kings, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, son of the charioteer, along with our own chief warriors,
gita-11-26.meaning: Arjuna sees the warriors of both armies rushing into God's form.
gita-11-26.explanation: Arjuna now sees the very warriors on the battlefield: the Kaurava princes, the allied kings, Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and leaders from his own side too. The sentence continues.

gita-11-27.translation: rush into your fearful mouths with their terrible tusks. Some are seen caught between your teeth, their heads crushed to powder.
gita-11-27.meaning: Arjuna sees the warriors entering God's mouths and being crushed, foreshadowing their deaths.
gita-11-27.explanation: Arjuna sees the warriors rushing into the terrible mouths. Some are caught between the teeth, their heads crushed. It is a vision of the coming destruction of the war.

gita-11-28.translation: As the many currents of rivers rush toward the ocean, so these heroes of the world of men enter your blazing mouths.
gita-11-28.meaning: Like rivers flowing into the sea, the warriors flow into God.
gita-11-28.explanation: Arjuna uses an image of nature. Just as rivers rush unstoppably to the ocean, these great warriors pour into Krishna's flaming mouths.

gita-11-29.translation: As moths fly at great speed into a blazing flame to their destruction, so these beings rush at great speed into your mouths to their destruction.
gita-11-29.meaning: Like moths flying into a flame, the warriors rush toward their end.
gita-11-29.explanation: A second image: moths fly helplessly into fire and perish. So the warriors speed into Krishna's mouths and are destroyed.

gita-11-30.translation: Devouring all the worlds on every side with your flaming mouths, you lick your lips. Your fierce rays fill the whole universe with light and scorch it, Vishnu.
gita-11-30.meaning: God's flaming form seems to swallow all worlds and burn the universe.
gita-11-30.explanation: Arjuna sees Krishna consuming the worlds on every side. His fierce radiance fills and burns the entire universe.

gita-11-31.translation: Tell me who you are, with so fearsome a form. I bow to you, best of gods. Have mercy. I wish to know you, the original one, for I do not understand what you are doing.
gita-11-31.meaning: Arjuna begs to know who this awesome form is and what it is doing.
gita-11-31.explanation: Overwhelmed, Arjuna asks the most basic question: who are you? He bows, asks for mercy, and confesses he does not understand the purpose of this terrible activity.

gita-11-32.translation: Krishna said: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, now at work to wipe out these people. Even without you, none of these warriors arrayed in the opposing armies will survive.
gita-11-32.meaning: Krishna reveals himself as Time, which destroys all. The warriors will die whether Arjuna fights or not.
gita-11-32.explanation: Krishna answers: he is Kala, Time, the force that brings all things to an end. The warriors' fate is already sealed; even if Arjuna does not fight, they will not survive.

gita-11-33.translation: So stand up and win glory. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me. Be merely the instrument, Savyasachin.
gita-11-33.meaning: The outcome is already decided by God. Arjuna should act as God's instrument.
gita-11-33.explanation: Krishna tells Arjuna to rise and gain honour. The deaths are already accomplished by Time; Arjuna is only to be the instrument. Savyasachin means one who can shoot with either hand.

gita-11-34.translation: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and the other great warriors have already been slain by me. Kill them, do not be troubled. Fight, and you will defeat your rivals in battle.
gita-11-34.meaning: Even the greatest warriors are already doomed. Arjuna should fight without fear.
gita-11-34.explanation: Krishna names the most feared warriors on the other side: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha and Karna. They are already destroyed by him, so Arjuna need not be afraid.

gita-11-35.translation: Sanjaya said: Hearing these words of Keshava, the crowned Arjuna, trembling, joined his palms and bowed. Bowing again, overcome with fear, he spoke to Krishna in a faltering voice.
gita-11-35.meaning: Shaken, Arjuna bowed again and again and spoke with a trembling voice.
gita-11-35.explanation: Sanjaya describes Arjuna's state. Trembling, with hands joined, bowing repeatedly and full of fear, he speaks to Krishna with a choked voice.

gita-11-36.translation: Arjuna said: It is right, Hrishikesha, that the world delights and rejoices in your praise. The demons flee in fear in every direction, and the hosts of perfected beings bow to you.
gita-11-36.meaning: The good rejoice in God, while evil runs from him in fear.
gita-11-36.explanation: Arjuna praises Krishna again. It is fitting that the world takes joy in praising him. Evil beings scatter in fear, while the perfected ones bow down.

keywords.meaning: flee in fear in all directions

gita-11-37.translation: And why should they not bow to you, great soul, who are greater even than Brahma, the first creator? Infinite Lord of gods, home of the universe, you are the imperishable, being and non-being, and what is beyond both.
gita-11-37.meaning: God is greater than the creator himself, the home of all, beyond being and non-being.
gita-11-37.explanation: Arjuna asks why the beings would not bow, since Krishna is greater even than Brahma, the original creator. He is infinite and imperishable, both being and non-being, and beyond them.

gita-11-38.translation: You are the first God, the ancient Person, the final resting place of this universe. You are the knower and the known, and the supreme abode. By you the universe is pervaded, infinite one.
gita-11-38.meaning: God is the first being, the knower and what is known, and he fills the universe.
gita-11-38.explanation: Arjuna continues his hymn: Krishna is the original God and the ancient Person, the ultimate support of the world, both the one who knows and what is known, the highest home.

gita-11-39.translation: You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati and the great-grandfather. Salutations to you, a thousand salutations, and again and again, salutations to you!
gita-11-39.meaning: God is all the gods. Arjuna bows to him again and again.
gita-11-39.explanation: Arjuna names the great gods of wind, death, fire, water and the moon, and the creator, and says Krishna is all of them. He then bows again and again.

gita-11-40.translation: Salutations to you in front and behind, salutations to you on every side, O All. Your power is infinite and your strength measureless. You pervade everything, and so you are everything.
gita-11-40.meaning: God is on every side, infinite in power, and so he is everything.
gita-11-40.explanation: Arjuna bows in every direction, because Krishna is everywhere. His strength and courage have no limit, and because he pervades all, he is all.

gita-11-41.translation: Thinking of you only as a friend, whatever I said rashly, 'O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend,' not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or love,
gita-11-41.meaning: Arjuna remembers how casually he treated Krishna as a friend, not knowing his greatness.
gita-11-41.explanation: Arjuna remembers years of friendship in which he called Krishna by familiar names without knowing his true greatness. The sentence continues in the next verse.

keywords.meaning: thinking of you as a friend

gita-11-42.translation: and if, in jest, I was disrespectful to you while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in company, I ask your forgiveness, immeasurable one.
gita-11-42.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to forgive any disrespect shown in their everyday friendship.
gita-11-42.explanation: Arjuna asks forgiveness for any jokes or casual disrespect while playing, resting, sitting or eating, whether alone or with others.

gita-11-43.translation: You are the father of the world, of all that moves and does not move. You are its worshipful teacher, greater than any teacher. No one equals you in the three worlds; how could anyone surpass you, whose power is beyond compare?
gita-11-43.meaning: God is the father of all and the greatest teacher, without equal.
gita-11-43.explanation: Arjuna calls Krishna the father of all beings and the most revered guru. No one is equal to him, let alone greater.

gita-11-44.translation: So I bow down and lay my body before you, asking your grace, adorable Lord. Bear with me, God, as a father with his son, a friend with his friend, a lover with the beloved.
gita-11-44.meaning: Arjuna asks God to forgive him the way a father, friend or loved one would.
gita-11-44.explanation: Arjuna prostrates himself and asks Krishna to be patient with him, as a father is with a child, a friend with a friend, or a lover with a beloved.

keywords.meaning: as a father with a son
as a friend with a friend
as a lover with the beloved

gita-11-45.translation: I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, but my mind is shaken with fear. Show me your other form, Lord. Have mercy, Lord of gods, home of the universe.
gita-11-45.meaning: Arjuna is overjoyed yet afraid, and asks to see Krishna's familiar form again.
gita-11-45.explanation: Arjuna feels both joy at this unprecedented vision and fear. He asks Krishna to return to his gentler form.

gita-11-46.translation: I want to see you as before, with crown, mace and discus in hand. Take on your four-armed form, thousand-armed one, whose form is the universe.
gita-11-46.meaning: Arjuna asks to see Krishna's four-armed form, gentle and familiar.
gita-11-46.explanation: Arjuna asks to see Krishna in the four-armed form of Vishnu, holding mace and discus and wearing a crown, rather than the overwhelming thousand-armed cosmic form.

gita-11-47.translation: Krishna said: By my grace, Arjuna, through my own power, I have shown you this supreme form, full of light, universal, infinite and original, which no one but you has seen before.
gita-11-47.meaning: Krishna says he showed this form out of grace, and no one else has ever seen it.
gita-11-47.explanation: Krishna reassures Arjuna. The vision was a gift of grace, shown by Krishna's own yogic power. Its brilliance and infinity have never been seen by anyone else.

gita-11-48.translation: Not by the Vedas, sacrifices or study, not by charity, rituals or harsh austerities can I be seen in this form in the world of men by anyone but you, great hero of the Kurus.
gita-11-48.meaning: No ritual, study or penance can earn this vision. It is a gift.
gita-11-48.explanation: Krishna stresses that none of the usual religious means, not scripture, ritual, giving or austerity, can produce this vision. It came to Arjuna alone.

gita-11-49.translation: Do not be afraid or bewildered at seeing this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and glad at heart, see again my familiar form.
gita-11-49.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna not to be afraid and shows his gentle form again.
gita-11-49.explanation: Krishna comforts Arjuna. He should not be shaken by the terrible vision. Let go of fear, be glad, and see Krishna's familiar form once more.

gita-11-50.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this way to Arjuna, Vasudeva showed his own form again. Taking on his gentle form once more, the great one comforted the frightened Arjuna.
gita-11-50.meaning: Krishna returned to his gentle human form and comforted Arjuna.
gita-11-50.explanation: Sanjaya reports that Krishna showed his own form again, the gentle and pleasing one, and calmed the terrified Arjuna.

gita-11-51.translation: Arjuna said: Seeing this gentle human form of yours, Janardana, I am now calm and myself again.
gita-11-51.meaning: Seeing Krishna in human form again, Arjuna feels calm and himself once more.
gita-11-51.explanation: Seeing Krishna's familiar human form, Arjuna recovers. His mind settles and he returns to his normal state.

gita-11-52.translation: Krishna said: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see. Even the gods always long to see it.
gita-11-52.meaning: Few ever see this form. Even the gods long for it.
gita-11-52.explanation: Krishna stresses how rare Arjuna's vision was. Even the gods yearn constantly to see this form.

gita-11-53.translation: Not by the Vedas, not by austerity, not by charity, not by sacrifice can I be seen as you have seen me.
gita-11-53.meaning: No scripture, penance, gift or ritual can bring this vision.
gita-11-53.explanation: Krishna repeats that the vision cannot be gained through scripture study, austerities, charity or sacrifice.

gita-11-54.translation: But by devotion to me alone, Arjuna, I can be known in this way, seen as I truly am, and entered into, scorcher of foes.
gita-11-54.meaning: Only wholehearted love lets you know God, see him truly and become one with him.
gita-11-54.explanation: Krishna names the one way: ananya bhakti, undivided devotion. By it he can be known, seen in truth and entered into.

gita-11-55.translation: One who works for me, who holds me as the highest goal, who is devoted to me, free from attachment and without hatred toward any being, comes to me, Pandava.
gita-11-55.meaning: Work for God, make him your goal, love him, let go of clinging and hate no one. Then you reach him.
gita-11-55.explanation: This verse is often called the essence of the Gita. Its five marks are: doing one's work for God, making God the goal, devotion, freedom from attachment, and having no enmity toward any creature.

gita-12-1.translation: Arjuna said: Some devotees stay always devoted and worship You. Others worship the imperishable, unseen Absolute. Which of these knows yoga best?
gita-12-1.meaning: Arjuna asks a simple question: is it better to love God in a personal form, or to seek the formless, unseen Truth?
gita-12-1.explanation: Chapter 11 ended with Krishna showing Arjuna his cosmic form and praising loving devotion. Arjuna now opens the chapter on devotion with a practical question. Some seekers worship Krishna as a personal God; others meditate on the formless, imperishable Brahman. Which path is better? The whole of chapter 12 is Krishna's answer, and it ends with a portrait of the devotee he loves most.

gita-12-2.translation: The Lord said: Those who fix their minds on Me, worship Me with constant devotion and are filled with the highest faith, I consider the most perfect in yoga.
gita-12-2.meaning: Krishna answers: those who lovingly keep their mind on him, with deep faith, are the most perfect in yoga.
gita-12-2.explanation: Krishna's first answer favours the path of personal devotion. The key words are 'mind fixed on Me', 'always' and 'supreme faith'. Devotion here is not a ritual done now and then but a steady turning of the whole mind toward God. This verse sets the tone for the chapter: love and faith, kept up every day, are the surest way to union.

gita-12-3.translation: But those who worship the imperishable, which cannot be described, is unseen, everywhere present, beyond thought, unchanging, unmoving and eternal,
gita-12-3.meaning: Krishna turns to those who meditate on the formless Absolute, which no words or thoughts can capture.
gita-12-3.explanation: Here Krishna describes the second kind of seeker from Arjuna's question. Their object of worship is the imperishable Brahman, and Krishna lists its qualities: it cannot be defined, cannot be seen, is present everywhere, cannot be grasped by thought, and never changes. The sentence continues into the next verse, which says what becomes of these seekers.

gita-12-4.translation: restraining all their senses, even-minded everywhere, and delighting in the good of all beings, they too reach Me.
gita-12-4.meaning: People who seek the formless Truth also reach God, if they control their senses, stay balanced, and care for the welfare of everyone.
gita-12-4.explanation: Completing the previous verse, Krishna does not reject the path of the formless. Those who follow it also reach him. But he names what it demands: mastery of the senses, an even mind in every situation, and active joy in the welfare of all beings. The phrase 'delighting in the good of all' shows that even the most inward path must include care for others.

gita-12-5.translation: The struggle is greater for those whose minds cling to the unseen, for the goal of the unseen is hard for embodied beings to reach.
gita-12-5.meaning: The formless path is harder, because people living in bodies find it difficult to love what they cannot see or picture.
gita-12-5.explanation: Krishna explains why he called the devotees of a personal God 'most perfect'. Both paths lead to him, but for people with bodies and senses, an abstract, formless goal is hard to hold on to. The heart finds it easier to love a form it can picture and speak to. This is a gentle, practical teaching: choose the path you can actually walk.

gita-12-6.translation: But those who offer all their actions to Me, hold Me as their highest goal, and worship Me, meditating on Me with single-minded yoga,
gita-12-6.meaning: Krishna describes true devotees: they offer everything they do to God and think of him with undivided attention.
gita-12-6.explanation: This verse begins a two-verse promise. The devotee Krishna has in mind does not withdraw from life; they keep acting, but they hand over every action to God. Their attention is 'without another', meaning nothing competes with God for first place in their heart. The next verse says what Krishna does for such people.

gita-12-7.translation: for those whose minds are absorbed in Me, O Partha, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth.
gita-12-7.meaning: God himself quickly rescues those whose hearts are fixed on him from the endless cycle of birth and death.
gita-12-7.explanation: This is one of the warmest promises in the Gita. Life in the cycle of birth and death is pictured as a vast ocean. Krishna does not only show the way across; he says he personally becomes the rescuer who pulls the devotee out, and does so 'before long'. The condition is simple: a mind that has entered into God.

keywords.meaning: the one who lifts out, the rescuer
the ocean of death and repeated birth

gita-12-8.translation: Fix your mind on Me alone, let your understanding enter into Me. Then you will live in Me from now on; there is no doubt about this.
gita-12-8.meaning: Krishna's direct advice: put your mind and your understanding in God, and you will truly live in him.
gita-12-8.explanation: Having described the ideal, Krishna now speaks directly to Arjuna. He names two things to give: the mind, which feels and wants, and the buddhi, the intellect that decides. When both rest in God, the result is certain: 'you will dwell in Me'. This verse starts a ladder of practices; the following verses offer easier steps for anyone who finds this one too hard.

gita-12-9.translation: If you cannot hold your mind steadily on Me, then seek to reach Me through the yoga of practice, O Dhananjaya.
gita-12-9.meaning: If you can't keep your mind on God yet, don't give up: practise, again and again.
gita-12-9.explanation: Krishna is realistic. Holding the mind steady on God is hard, and he does not shame Arjuna for possibly failing. Instead he offers the next step: abhyāsa, repeated practice. Each time the mind wanders, bring it back. Steady effort, not instant perfection, is what he asks.

keywords.meaning: winner of wealth, a name of Arjuna

gita-12-10.translation: If you are unable even to practise, make working for Me your highest aim. Even by doing actions for My sake, you will reach perfection.
gita-12-10.meaning: If regular practice is too hard, simply do your work as an offering to God; that alone can lead you to perfection.
gita-12-10.explanation: The ladder comes down another step. Not everyone can sit and practise concentration. For them, Krishna offers service: do your ordinary work, but do it for God. Cooking, teaching, building or caring for others becomes worship when done with this intention. Krishna promises that this path, too, leads to perfection.

keywords.meaning: work for Me, service to God

gita-12-11.translation: If you cannot do even this, then take refuge in Me, control yourself, and give up the fruits of all your actions.
gita-12-11.meaning: If even working for God is too hard, just do your best and let go of worrying about the results.
gita-12-11.explanation: This is the last and most accessible step on the ladder. Even someone who cannot think of God while working can practise letting go: do the right thing, then release your grip on how it turns out. This echoes the Gita's famous teaching on action without attachment to results, and shows that it is open to anyone.

keywords.meaning: giving up the fruits of action

gita-12-12.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruits of action is better than meditation, for peace follows immediately from giving them up.
gita-12-12.meaning: Letting go of the results of what you do brings peace right away; that's why Krishna rates it so highly.
gita-12-12.explanation: Krishna sums up the ladder in a surprising way. One might expect meditation to be the highest, but he places giving up the fruits of action above it, because peace follows at once. Whatever else we practise, if we still cling to outcomes we stay anxious. When the clinging goes, calm arrives. The verse links devotion to the Gita's teaching on selfless action.

gita-12-14.translation: Always content, steady in yoga, self-controlled and firm in resolve, with mind and understanding offered to Me, that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.
gita-12-14.meaning: The person God loves is content, disciplined, determined, and has given their heart and mind to him.
gita-12-14.explanation: Verses 13 to 19 paint a portrait of the devotee Krishna holds dear. This verse adds contentment, self-control and firm resolve to the friendliness and compassion of verse 13. The refrain 'he is dear to Me' recurs through the passage, showing that these qualities are not rules to earn love but the natural signs of a heart turned toward God.

gita-12-15.translation: One who does not disturb the world and is not disturbed by the world, who is free from excitement, impatience, fear and anxiety, is dear to Me.
gita-12-15.meaning: God loves the person who upsets no one, isn't easily upset, and stays free of over-excitement, fear and anxiety.
gita-12-15.explanation: This verse describes a two-way peace. Such a person causes no distress to others, and others cannot easily throw them off balance. Krishna lists the storms they are free of: sudden elation, impatience or intolerance, fear, and agitation. It is a picture of someone safe to be around and calm within.

keywords.meaning: to be disturbed, to shrink from

gita-12-16.translation: One who expects nothing, is pure and capable, unconcerned and untroubled, and has given up every selfish undertaking, that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.
gita-12-16.meaning: God loves the person who wants nothing in return, stays pure and skilful, and doesn't chase self-centred projects.
gita-12-16.explanation: The portrait continues. 'Expecting nothing' does not mean doing nothing: Krishna also calls this devotee dakṣa, skilful and capable. They act well, but without worry and without schemes driven by personal gain. Being both capable and free from craving is a balance the Gita returns to again and again.

keywords.meaning: one who has given up all (selfish) undertakings

gita-12-17.translation: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has let go of both good and bad outcomes and is full of devotion, is dear to Me.
gita-12-17.meaning: God loves the person who isn't carried away by happiness or hatred, sorrow or craving, and simply stays devoted.
gita-12-17.explanation: Krishna names four powerful pulls: excited joy, hatred, grief and craving. The devotee does not swing between them. 'Letting go of good and bad' means not clinging to pleasant outcomes or fleeing unpleasant ones. What remains in their place is devotion, steady and quiet, and that is what makes this person dear to God.

gita-12-18.translation: Alike toward enemy and friend, alike in honour and insult, alike in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and free from attachment,
gita-12-18.meaning: The devotee treats friend and enemy the same, and stays steady through praise and insult, comfort and hardship.
gita-12-18.explanation: Krishna lists the pairs of opposites that shake most people: friend and foe, honour and dishonour, cold and heat, pleasure and pain. The devotee meets each with the same even mind. This is not coldness; it is freedom from being tossed about. The sentence runs on into the next verse, which completes the description.

gita-12-19.translation: who takes blame and praise alike, speaks little, is content with whatever comes, has no fixed home, is steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to Me.
gita-12-19.meaning: God loves the one who stays the same under praise or blame, is content with whatever life brings, and keeps a steady, devoted mind.
gita-12-19.explanation: The portrait ends here. The devotee is unmoved by criticism or flattery, is quiet rather than talkative, and is satisfied with whatever comes their way. 'Without a home' can mean a wandering monk, but more deeply it means not clinging to any place or possession as one's security. Their only fixed point is a steady, devoted mind.

keywords.meaning: homeless, not attached to a dwelling

gita-12-20.translation: But those who follow this immortal teaching of dharma as I have described it, full of faith and holding Me as the highest, these devotees are exceedingly dear to Me.
gita-12-20.meaning: Krishna closes the chapter: those who live this teaching with faith are more dear to him than anyone.
gita-12-20.explanation: The final verse of the chapter turns the portrait into an invitation. Krishna calls what he has just described an 'immortal dharma', a way of living that leads beyond death. Those who take it up with faith, putting God first, are not just dear to him but 'exceedingly dear'. The chapter that began with a question about methods ends with a promise of love.
